The verse says that Allah loves those who are just in their judgement, even when the matter is between their enemies. The material links this to the reward that Allah gives to those who judge fairly.

### The background of the judgement

The material explains the case of the blood money between Banu Nadir and Banu Qurayzah in more detail. Banu Nadir took more blood money than Banu Qurayzah, and the people of Banu Qurayzah refused to accept the difference any longer. The report says that Ibn 'Abbas linked the verse to this dispute. In another report, Abu Dawud and al-Bukhari record that a Jewish case reached the Prophet ﷺ, and the Torah was opened to show that its punishment for adultery was stoning. The material says that the man who hid the verse with his hand was exposed by Abdullah bin Salam, and the Prophet ﷺ ordered the stoning.

The material gives the report that Ibn 'Umar was among those who stoned the Jewish adulterers and saw the man shielding the woman with his body. It also gives the report of al-Bara' bin Azib, which describes the Jewish man flogged and blackened with coal, and the Prophet ﷺ saying that he was the first to bring back the command that had been set aside.

### The two options and the abrogation

The material says that the choice in this verse was later replaced by the command to judge with what Allah has revealed. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah and As-Suddi are reported as holding that the choice was abrogated. The material notes that the subject of judgement under a pact was discussed in the previous entry, and that the Prophet ﷺ decided the cases of non-Muslims by the law revealed to him.

### In short

- The verse names two faults, listening to falsehood and taking forbidden gain.
- The Prophet ﷺ was given a choice to judge or to turn away, and the material records that this choice was later replaced by the command to judge.
- Where he judges, he must judge with justice, which Allah loves.

43.text:
"But why do they come to you for judgment when they ˹already˺ have the Torah containing Allah's judgment, then they turn away after all? They are not ˹true˺ believers"

This verse is a rebuke. It asks why people who have the Torah would come to the Prophet ﷺ for a judgement and then reject it. The material reads the question as an expression of wonder at their behaviour.

### Phrase by phrase

**"But why do they come to you for judgment?"** The material explains that this question is asked in amazement, and that the purpose of asking was not to find the truth. They wanted a lighter punishment, and they hoped the Prophet ﷺ would agree with their desires.

**"When they already have the Torah containing Allah's judgment."** The material says the Torah is in their hands, and the judgement of stoning for adultery is written in it. They could have followed it, and the verse shows that they had the answer already.

**"Then they turn away after all."** The material says that they turned away from the ruling of the Prophet ﷺ when it did not suit them. They came with a desire to be judged in their favour, and they abandoned his judgement when it went against them. The material notes that this is the act of people who follow their desires.

**"They are not true believers."** The material says that the rejection of the judgement is a sign that their faith is not true. The verse does not say they are unbelievers in every sense. It says they are not believers in the way they claim to be, since their conduct shows that they do not follow what they hold to be true.

### The lesson for the believers

The material draws a lesson for every Muslim who asks for a religious ruling. The one who seeks a fatwa must seek the command of Allah and His Messenger and follow it. A person who goes from one scholar to another until he finds an answer that suits him is following his own desires. The material says the verse warns against this, and that it is a way of following Shaytan.

### In short

- The verse asks in wonder why people with the Torah go to the Prophet ﷺ and then reject what he rules.
- They came seeking a lighter verdict, not the truth, and the material says that this shows their faith is not true.
- Anyone who seeks a ruling must seek the command of Allah and follow it, and not choose the verdict that suits his desire.

44.text:
"Indeed, We revealed the Torah, containing guidance and light, by which the prophets, who submitted themselves to Allah, made judgments for Jews. So too did the rabbis and scholars judge according to Allah's Book, with which they were entrusted and of which they were made keepers. So do not fear the people; fear Me! Nor trade my revelations for a fleeting gain. And those who do not judge by what Allah has revealed are ˹truly˺ the disbelievers"

This verse describes the Torah as guidance and light, and it names the people who were entrusted with its judgement. It then warns against fear of people and against trading the revelations for a small gain. It ends with a judgement on those who do not rule by what Allah has revealed.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, We revealed the Torah, containing guidance and light."** The material explains that the Torah was guidance, that it showed the path away from error, and that it was light that moved the heart. The material says the abrogation of the Torah's law at a later time was not a fault in the Torah. It was done because the rules were to change with the times, and the same Revealer sent both books.

**"By which the prophets, who submitted themselves to Allah, made judgments for Jews."** The material says the prophets who came after Musa, up to the time of Jesus, judged the Jews by the Torah. The material mentions that this period had many prophets.

**"So too did the rabbis and scholars judge according to Allah's Book."** The material explains the two groups. The Rabbaniyyun are the people of Allah who are devoted to worship and remembrance and who have the knowledge they need. The Ahbar are scholars who know the rules and teach them. The material says the two names are different because a person is named after his main activity, but that a true man of Allah must be a scholar, and a true scholar must act on his knowledge. The material links the Ahbar to the Ulama and the Rabbaniyyun to the Mashaikh, and it says that there is no real split between the two.

**"With which they were entrusted and of which they were made keepers."** The material says the scholars were given the protection of the Book of Allah and were made its guardians, so they were to enforce it and not change it.

**"So do not fear the people; fear Me."** The material explains that the Jews were told not to fear the loss of their followers or the anger of their people. Their fear of Allah should be greater than their fear of people, and they should not change the law for worldly gain. The material says the warning is also given to the Muslims, to keep them from altering the law out of greed for money or position.

**"Nor trade My revelations for a fleeting gain."** The material links this to the rule against taking a paltry price in exchange for the truth. The scholars had made it a habit to bend the rules for influential people in return for payment, and the verse condemns it.

**"And those who do not judge by what Allah has revealed are truly the disbelievers."** The material says that the verse distinguishes between different kinds of disbelief. Ibn 'Abbas said that rejecting what Allah has revealed is kufr, while rejecting it without rejecting Allah is a lesser kind. Ibn Tawus added that it is not the kind that puts a person outside the religion, and 'Ata' said there are degrees of kufr. Abu Hanifah and other jurists read the verse as applying to the Jews. The material records that Al-Hasan al-Basri added that it applies to the Muslims too.

### The trade of the revelations

The material explains that the scholars of the Jews traded the revelation for worldly gain in more than one way. Some took direct bribes for false rulings. Others changed the rules to suit popular tastes, because a religion that asks for nothing of the believer is popular and draws crowds. The material says the greater danger is the second kind, because it is hidden behind respect and public admiration. The material says a religion that gives sanctity to national or communal interests without any demand for true obedience is one of the traps the verse warns about.

### In short

- The Torah was guidance and light, and the prophets and scholars judged by it because they were entrusted with its protection.
- The believers must not fear people more than Allah, and must not trade His revelations for worldly gain.
- Failing to judge by what Allah has revealed is kufr, though the scholars differ on whether it is the kind that takes a person out of the religion.

45.text:
"We ordained for them in the Torah, “A life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth—and for wounds equal retaliation.” But whoever waives it charitably, it will be atonement for them. And those who do not judge by what Allah has revealed are ˹truly˺ the wrongdoers"

This verse states the law of equal retaliation, qisas, as it was given in the Torah. It applies that law to killing and to bodily injury. It then praises the one who forgives, and calls those who do not rule by Allah's revelation wrongdoers. The material reads the verse as a rebuke to the Jews, who applied the Torah's law selectively.

### Phrase by phrase

**"We ordained for them in the Torah."** The material explains that the Torah contained this law from the start, and that the Jews had it in their own book. The verse is a reminder that they could not claim to be ignorant of it.

**"A life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth."** The material explains that each phrase is a rule of equal retaliation for a deliberate injury. Ibn 'Abbas read the phrases as they were applied in the Torah, so that a life taken is answered by a life, and each limb by the same limb.

**"And for wounds equal retaliation."** The material says that a wound is answered by an equal wound, where that is possible. Where it is not possible, the matter is left to the judge and to arbitration. The material says the rule for wounds is the same for free Muslims and for their slaves, men and women alike.

**"But whoever waives it charitably, it will be atonement for them."** The material explains that the waiver is an act of charity. It is an expiation for the one who forgives and a reward for the victim. Ibn 'Abbas, Jabir bin 'Abdullah, Al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibrahim An-Nakha'i and Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani all held this view. The material records a hadith from Ubadah bin As-Samit that whoever suffers a wound and forgoes his right of retaliation will be pardoned for a similar sin. An-Nasa'i and Ibn Jarir recorded it.

**"And those who do not judge by what Allah has revealed are truly the wrongdoers."** The material says the Jews rejected the law of the Torah when it did not suit them. They applied retaliation only when a man of Banu Nadir was killed by a man of Banu Qurayzah, and paid blood money in the reverse case. The verse calls this injustice.

### The case of Banu Nadir and Banu Qurayzah

The material explains that the two tribes had a harsh pact. If a man of Banu Qurayzah killed a man of Banu Nadir, the killer was put to death, and blood money was also taken. If a man of Banu Nadir killed a man of Banu Qurayzah, only blood money was due, and it was half the amount. The verse exposes this unfairness by showing that the same rule of equality was in their own Torah.

### Equality of the killer and the victim

The material records that the scholars agree that this verse is to be enforced. The imams agree that a man is killed for a woman he kills, based on the general sense of the verse. An-Nasa'i records a letter that the Prophet ﷺ gave to Amr bin Hazm, which says that a man is killed for a woman. Another hadith says that Muslims are equal in the sanctity of their blood. The majority of the scholars hold this view.

The material gives a hadith from Anas bin Malik, which Ahmad recorded. Ar-Rabi, the aunt of Anas, broke the tooth of a girl. The family of the girl refused to forgive, and went to the Prophet ﷺ, who ordered retaliation. Anas bin An-Nadr, the brother of the girl, asked whether the tooth of Ar-Rabi would be broken, and the Prophet ﷺ said the Book of Allah prescribes retaliation. The girl's family then forgave her. The Prophet ﷺ said that there are some servants of Allah who, if they swear by Allah, will have their oath fulfilled. The hadith is recorded in the two sahihs.

### Wounds and the waiting period

The material says that retaliation for a wound must not be carried out until the wound has healed. A report from Amr bin Shu'ayb, from his father and grandfather, which Ahmad recorded, tells of a man who stabbed another in the leg. The Prophet ﷺ told the victim to wait until he healed. He did not wait, and the retaliation went ahead. He then limped, and the Prophet ﷺ said that the limp had no compensation because he had disobeyed. The Prophet ﷺ then forbade retaliation for a wound before it heals. The material says that if the victim takes retaliation and the aggressor dies from it, there is no compensation, according to the majority of the Companions and their followers.

### The reasons for the revelation

The material says that the verse is linked to the case of the Jewish tribes in the previous verses. The Torah's law of equal retaliation was ignored by the Jews, and so the verse reminds them of it. The material also says that the law of wounds and retaliation is a matter of justice, and that the law applies to all people without regard to their rank. Sometimes a person causes harm without any evil intent, under emotional pressure. In such cases the forgiveness of the victim is a form of magnanimity, and it builds a society that is broad-minded.

### In short

- The Torah ordained equal retaliation, and the verse uses this to expose the selective justice of the Jews.
- Forgiveness of a wound is an expiation for the one who forgives, and a reward for the victim.
- Retaliation for a wound must wait until it heals, and the one who rejects the law of Allah is a wrongdoer.

46.text:
"Then in the footsteps of the prophets, We sent Jesus, son of Mary, confirming the Torah revealed before him. And We gave him the Gospel containing guidance and light and confirming what was revealed in the Torah—a guide and a lesson to the God-fearing"

This verse moves from the Torah to the Gospel. It presents Jesus as a prophet who confirmed the Torah, and it gives the Gospel as a book of guidance and light. The verse prepares the ground for the call to judge by the Gospel in 5:47.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Then in the footsteps of the prophets, We sent Jesus, son of Mary."** The material explains that Isa came after the prophets of the Children of Israel. He is named as the son of Maryam, and the verse marks his place in the line of the prophets.

**"Confirming the Torah revealed before him."** The material says that he believed in the Torah and judged by it. The verse does not say he replaced it entirely. The material notes that in another verse Isa told the Children of Israel that he came to make lawful some of what had been forbidden to them, and the scholars say that the Gospel abrogated some rules of the Torah.

**"And We gave him the Gospel containing guidance and light."** The material explains that the Gospel is guidance to the truth and light that removes doubt and settles disputes. The Gospel also confirms the Torah, and in most of its rules it agrees with it.

**"A guide and a lesson to the God-fearing."** The material says that the Gospel warns against sin and error for those who have taqwa, and who fear the warning and punishment of Allah.

### The Gospel and the coming of Muhammad

The material says that the people of the Gospel were commanded to believe in all that it contains, including the good news of the coming of Muhammad ﷺ, and to follow him when he was sent. The verse about the Prophet in 7:157 is cited in the material to show that the Torah and the Gospel both described him.

### In short

- Isa came after the prophets of the Children of Israel, confirmed the Torah, and was given the Gospel.
- The Gospel was guidance and light, and it warned the God-fearing against sin.
- The people of the Gospel were commanded to believe in all of it, including the good news of the Prophet ﷺ.

47.text:
"So let the people of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed in it. And those who do not judge by what Allah has revealed are ˹truly˺ the rebellious"

This verse commands the people of the Gospel to judge by the revelation it contains. It names those who refuse as rebellious.

### Phrase by phrase

**"So let the people of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed in it."** The material explains that the command is for the people of the Gospel to follow its rules, and to believe in the good news it gives of Muhammad ﷺ. The material notes a reading that makes the verb a continuation of the earlier command to give the Gospel to Isa.

**"And those who do not judge by what Allah has revealed are truly the rebellious."** The material says the rebellious are those who reject the truth and prefer falsehood. The material says that this verse was revealed about the Christians, and that the context shows it.

### In short

- The people of the Gospel are commanded to judge by what Allah revealed in it.
- Those who refuse this command are rebellious, because they prefer falsehood to the truth.
- The verse is read with 5:45 and 5:46 as a judgement on the two groups of the People of the Book.

48.text:
"We have revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ this Book with the truth, as a confirmation of previous Scriptures and a supreme authority on them. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires over the truth that has come to you. To each of you We have ordained a code of law and a way of life. If Allah had willed, He would have made you one community, but His Will is to test you with what He has given ˹each of˺ you. So compete with one another in doing good. To Allah you will all return, then He will inform you ˹of the truth˺ regarding your differences"

This verse turns from the earlier books to the Qur'an. It says that the Qur'an came with the truth, confirms what was before it, and watches over it. It then commands the Prophet ﷺ to judge by what Allah has revealed and not by the desires of the People of the Book. The verse ends with a teaching about the differing laws of the prophets and a call to good deeds.

### Phrase by phrase

**"We have revealed to you this Book with the truth."** The material explains that the Qur'an is sent down with the truth, which comes from Allah and is beyond doubt. The word "with the truth" links the revelation to its source and to its content.

**"As a confirmation of previous Scriptures and a supreme authority on them."** The material gives several readings of the Arabic word translated as supreme authority. Ibn 'Abbas said it means trustworthy. Mujahid, Qatadah and As-Suddi read it as witness. Al-Awfi reported Ibn 'Abbas as saying it means dominant. The material says these meanings are close, and that together they show the Qur'an is trustworthy, a witness and dominant over every Scripture before it. Whatever in the earlier books agrees with the Qur'an is true, and whatever disagrees with it is false. The Qur'an alone preserves the original truth of those books, since the earlier bearers could not keep them intact. Allah promised to guard the Qur'an, as the verse of 15:9 states.

**"So judge between them by what Allah has revealed."** The material explains that the Prophet ﷺ was given the choice to judge or turn away when the Jews came to him, but the command in this verse is to judge by the Qur'an and by the law of the earlier prophets that the Qur'an approves. Ibn 'Abbas reported that the choice was replaced by this command.

**"And do not follow their desires over the truth that has come to you."** The material says that the desires in question are the ideas that turned the Jews away from what Allah had revealed. The verse warns the Prophet ﷺ not to move from the truth to suit them.

**"To each of you We have ordained a code of law and a way of life."** The material explains that the word for code is a clear path. Every prophet had a distinct law, and that law was partly or fully abrogated by the law of a later prophet. The law of Muhammad ﷺ is the last, and it abrogated all those before it.

**"If Allah had willed, He would have made you one community."** The material says this is a general statement of the power of Allah. He could have made all mankind follow one religion and one law that would never change. He chose different laws in order to test His servants in their obedience.

**"But His Will is to test you with what He has given each of you."** The material says the trial is in what has been given, which for the believers is the Book. The test is to see who obeys the command given to them at each time.

**"So compete with one another in doing good."** The material explains that the believers should race to good deeds, which are obedience to Allah and following the law of the final prophet. Ad-Dahhak read the address as directed to the community of Muhammad ﷺ, though the material says the wider sense is clearer.

**"To Allah you will all return, then He will inform you regarding your differences."** The material says the return is to Allah on the Day of Resurrection. Those who were sincere will be rewarded, and those who rejected the truth and turned to other paths without proof will be punished.

### The wisdom of the differing laws

The material gives a full answer to the question of why the laws of the prophets differ. The differences are in the subsidiary rules, while the principle of worship and obedience is the same. The material says that the true worship is in being a servant who obeys, and that prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, zakah, remembrance and recitation are means to that end and not ends in themselves. The material gives examples. Prayer is forbidden at certain times, and praying then is a sin. Fasting on the two Eids is forbidden, and it is a sin to fast on them. Gathering on the plain of Arafat is rewarded only on the ninth of Dhul-Hijjah. The same principle applies to every act of worship. When it is done as commanded, it is worship. When it is stopped at a certain limit, it becomes forbidden.

The material says that when people turn a habit or a custom into worship, they begin to ignore the open commands of Allah and His Messenger. This is how innovations enter the religion over time, and it was the main cause of the changes that happened to the earlier books.

The material gives a second reason for the difference. Human beings differ in temper and taste, and the times differ too, so the laws of the subsidiary rules were changed to suit the condition of the people. The material explains that abrogation is not a mistake or a change of mind by the Lawgiver. It is like the medicine a physician prescribes in stages, since the physician knows in advance what the patient will need.

The material also explains that the change of the qiblah shows this, as the verse of 2:143 makes clear. The Children of Israel were commanded to face Jerusalem in prayer, and they came to think that prayer meant facing Jerusalem. The qiblah was then changed to the Kabah, and the change showed who worshipped the building and who worshipped Allah. The material says that no prophet will come after Muhammad ﷺ, so such a change will not happen again. The true aim of worship remains the same, which is to turn to Allah directly with a mind free of outward ceremony.

### Musa, the Injil and the abrogated rules

The material says that Allah praised the Torah he sent down to Musa, the one He spoke to directly, and commanded its people to follow it until its law was abrogated. He then praised the Injil and commanded its people to follow it. The rules that were abrogated were not evil in their time. They were haram or halal according to the need of that time, and the change to a new law was a test of obedience. The material gives the example of the rule of qisas, which the Torah set out and the Qur'an kept. Ibn Zayd and As-Suddi are reported to have read the earlier laws in the same way, as stages in one religion. The material says that the rule of mansukh in the Qur'an means a rule that was replaced, and that replacement is itself the wisdom of the lawgiver.

### The Jews and the offer of conversion

The material explains that some Jewish leaders came to the Prophet ﷺ with an offer. They would become Muslims if he judged their case in their favour. The verse was revealed to warn him against deciding in such a way, and to command him to judge by the law of Allah with equity and justice. The material says the offer was not his concern.

### The summary of the lessons

The material lists five lessons from the verse. First, the rulings of an earlier law remain in force until the Qur'an abrogates them, as in the Torah's rule of equal retaliation and the stoning for adultery. Second, the rules of the earlier scriptures that the Qur'an did not abrogate are still binding. Third, judging against the law of Allah is kufr when a person believes it is false, and it is injustice or sin when he accepts it as true and still acts against it in practice. Fourth, taking a bribe is forbidden, and in a court case it is especially grave. Fifth, the prophets and their laws agree in principle, and differ in details for reasons of wisdom.

### In short

- The Qur'an came with the truth, confirms the earlier books, and watches over them.
- The Prophet ﷺ is commanded to judge by the law of Allah and not by the desires of the People of the Book.
- The different laws of the prophets test the people, and the true aim of worship is obedience to Allah.

49.text:
"And judge between them ˹O Prophet˺ by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires. And beware, so they do not lure you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. If they turn away ˹from Allah's judgment˺, then know that it is Allah's Will to repay them for some of their sins, and that many people are indeed rebellious"

This verse repeats the command to judge by the revelation and warns the Prophet ﷺ against being led away from it. It says that if the Jews turn away from the judgement, Allah will punish them for some of their sins, and that most people are rebellious.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires."** The material says this is a repeated command. The Prophet ﷺ is to judge by the law of Allah, and not by the wishes of the people who came to him. The material links this to the report that Ibn 'Abbas gave of the choice being replaced.

**"And beware, so they do not lure you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you."** The material explains that the Jews were enemies, and the warning is to beware of their plan. They wanted to lead the Prophet ﷺ away from part of the revelation, for example by setting aside the stoning for adultery. The material says that they were liars, treacherous and disbelievers.

**"If they turn away, then know that it is Allah's Will to repay them for some of their sins."** The material explains that their turning away was itself a sin, and that Allah's decree included punishment for their earlier sins. The material says the punishment in the world is for some of their sins, and the greater punishment is in the Hereafter.

**"And that many people are indeed rebellious."** The material says most people disobey their Lord and turn from the truth. It cites 12:103, which says that most people will not believe even if you desire it eagerly, and 6:116, which warns that following most of those on earth will lead one away from the path of Allah.

### The report of the four leaders

The material gives an account from Ibn Ishaq and Ibn 'Abbas. Ibn Zayd and Abu al-Yaman are also named in the reports on the trial of the Prophet ﷺ in this matter. Ka'b bin Asad, Ibn Suluba, Abdullah ibn Suriya and Shas bin Qays said to each other that they should go to Muhammad and try to lead him from his religion. They said that if he would rule in favour of them against their people, they would follow him, and the Jews would follow them. The Prophet ﷺ refused, and this verse was revealed. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim recorded the report.

### In short

- The Prophet ﷺ is commanded to judge by the revelation and not to follow the desires of the People of the Book.
- Their turning away is a sin, and Allah will punish them for some of their sins in this world and all of them in the Hereafter.
- Most people are rebellious, and the verse cites 12:103 and 6:116 in support.

50.text:
"Is it the judgment of ˹pre-Islamic˺ ignorance they seek? Who could be a better judge than Allah for people of sure faith"

This verse ends the passage with a question. It asks whether the people seek the judgement of the age of ignorance, and it says that no one is a better judge than Allah for those who are certain in their faith.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Is it the judgment of pre-Islamic ignorance they seek?"** The material explains that jahiliyyah is the age before Islam, when people ruled by opinion, desire and custom. The question is one of rebuke. The material says that those who turn away from the law of Allah are seeking this kind of judgement.

**"Who could be a better judge than Allah for people of sure faith?"** The material says that no one can judge better than Allah, who knows everything, can do all things, and is just. The people of sure faith are those who understand the law of Allah and are certain that He is the best judge, and that He is more merciful to His creation than a mother to her child.

### The rulings of custom

The material gives an example from later times. The Tatars followed the law that their king, Genghis Khan, wrote, called Al-Yasiq. It drew on rulings from several religions and from his own opinion and desires. The material says that whoever follows such laws over the law of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger is a disbeliever, and deserves to be fought until he returns to the judgement of Allah and His Messenger. The material also gives a hadith from al-Tabarani, which Abu al-Yaman narrated in a similar form in the collection of Al-Bukhari. Its warning is against the Muslim who goes after the customs of the age of ignorance, and against the one who spills blood without cause.

The material says the unseen matters of faith, which the people of sure faith accept, are the reason the verse speaks of them. Ibn Zayd read the verse as a warning to those who choose to reject the unseen.

### In short

- The question rebukes those who seek the judgement of the age of ignorance.
- Allah is the best judge for those who are certain of their faith, since He knows all and is more merciful than a mother to her child.
- Preferring a law of opinion or custom over the law of Allah is a grave error, and the material records a hadith against seeking the ways of ignorance.

51.text:
"O believers! Take neither Jews nor Christians as guardians—they are guardians of each other. Whoever does so will be counted as one of them. Surely Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people"

This verse forbids the believers from taking the Jews and Christians as close friends and protectors. The material explains that the verse does not forbid kindness and fair dealing with them. It forbids a deep and exclusive friendship that would blur the marks of Islam and place a believer's loyalty with those who oppose the community.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O believers!"** The address is to the community of faith. The material explains that the command to keep distance in friendship is a matter for the Muslims as a community, which must keep its own bonds and its own protection.

**"Take neither Jews nor Christians as guardians."** The Arabic word is awliya, which means close friends, allies and protectors. The material calls the forbidden friendship al-Muwalat, a deep and intimate bond. It notes that Muslims may deal with non-Muslims in justice, kindness and goodwill, and may trade and live alongside them. What is not allowed is the kind of intimacy that makes a person lean on them for support against the community.

**"They are guardians of each other."** The material explains that Jews and Christians tend to reserve their deep loyalty for their own people, so an alliance with a Muslim would be against their own customs. The verse says they stand together against the believers, and a Muslim who joins them stands on their side.

**"Whoever does so will be counted as one of them."** The material says that a Muslim who makes such an alliance is counted with them in the sight of Islam, and is not a true Muslim in that relationship. It cites Ibn Jarir for the reading that this is about a particular case of alliance.

**"Surely Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."** The material says that those who take the enemies of the community as protectors are doing wrong, and that the one who does wrong is not guided to the path of faith in that matter.

### The background

The material gives the reason for the verse as the treaty the Prophet ﷺ made with the Jews and Christians near Madinah. They agreed not to fight the Muslims or help their enemies, and to join the Muslims in defence of Madinah. The Jews of Banu Qurayzah broke the treaty. They secretly agreed with the pagans of Makkah against the Muslims and sent them a letter inviting them to their fortress. When the Prophet ﷺ learned of this plot, he sent a group of fighters to confront them. Some of the Jews had also made friendships with Muslims, and used these bonds to pass information to Makkah.

The material says that this verse stopped the Muslims from such friendships, so that the enemy would not learn their secrets. Ubadah bin al-Samit openly cancelled his treaty obligations to the Jews and announced that he would have no close friendship with them. Abdullah bin Ubayy, the hypocrite, said he feared the danger of cutting the bond, and so he refused to do so.

### Commentary on the principle

The material gives three principles from the verse. The first is that Muslims may treat non-Muslims with tolerance, justice and kindness, but not with deep friendship. The second is that if some Muslims drift into such friendship, the religion is not harmed by it, since Allah has taken responsibility for protecting Islam. If a people turns away and leaves the faith, Allah will raise another people to uphold its law. The third is that the true and deep friendship of a Muslim is with Allah, His Messenger and those who believe.

The material also notes the position of the Muslims in Arabia at the time. The Jews and Christians held much of the economic power, and many weaker Muslims lived in dual loyalty out of fear of them. The material says that worshipping the truth only in unimportant matters does not help a person when danger comes, since he will meet the fate of those he supported.

### Umar and the Christian scribe

The material gives an example of the rule in this verse from the time of Umar. Umar asked Abu Musa al-Ash'ari to send him a written account of the money received and spent. Abu Musa had a Christian scribe prepare it, and Umar was pleased with the work. He asked whether the scribe could read a letter that had come from Ash-Sham to the mosque. Abu Musa said he could not, and that the scribe was a Christian. Umar rebuked him and told him to send the man out of Madinah. Umar then recited the verse. The material records a report from Abdullah bin Utbah that a person should be careful, since he may be a Jew or a Christian without knowing it, and that this was understood as a reference to this verse.

### The greater enemy

The material says that the greatest enemy of a believer is his own self. It cites the story of Joseph, who was thrown into a well, sold into slavery and kept in prison for years, and who never complained as he did about the soul that commands to evil, as stated in 12:53. The material also records the Prophet ﷺ describing the self that lies between a person's two sides as the worst enemy. The verse on friendship is therefore also a warning to guard against the desires of the self.

### In short

- Muslims may deal with Jews and Christians in justice and kindness, but they must not take them as deep allies against the community.
- The verse was revealed after the Jews of Banu Qurayzah broke their treaty and passed secrets to the enemy.
- The true friendship of a believer is with Allah, His Messenger and the believers.

52.text:
"You see those with sickness in their hearts racing for their guardianship, saying ˹in justification˺, “We fear a turn of fortune will strike us.” But perhaps Allah will bring about ˹your˺ victory or another favour by His command, and they will regret what they have hidden in their hearts"

This verse describes those with sickness in their hearts, the hypocrites, who rushed to make friends with the Jews and Christians. It records their excuse, and it promises that Allah may bring victory or His command, which will expose what they hid and bring their regret.

### Phrase by phrase

**"You see those with sickness in their hearts."** The material explains that the sickness is doubt, hesitation and hypocrisy. The verse refers to people like Abdullah bin Ubayy and his followers, who professed Islam outwardly and kept their true loyalty hidden.

**"Racing for their guardianship."** The material says that they hurried to offer their friendship and alliance to the Jews and Christians, in public and in secret. The verse uses the word race to show how eager they were.

**"Saying, 'We fear a turn of fortune will strike us.'"** The material says that they offered this as an excuse. They feared that the enemies of Islam might win, and so they wanted to be on good terms with the Jews and Christians, so that they could use that favour for their own benefit if the Muslims lost. The material notes that this fear is a sign of weak faith, since it puts worldly safety above obedience to Allah.

**"But perhaps Allah will bring about your victory or another favour by His command."** The material says that the victory in view is the conquest of Makkah, according to As-Suddi. The other favour is the command to make the Jews and Christians pay the jizyah, which is also reported from As-Suddi. The word perhaps, when spoken of Allah, expresses a certainty that the outcome will come about.

**"And they will regret what they have hidden in their hearts."** The material explains that the hypocrites will regret their friendship with the Jews and Christians, which did not protect them. It says Allah exposed their true state to the believers in this life, though they tried to hide it.

### In short

- The people with sickness in their hearts rushed to befriend the Jews and Christians out of fear for their own safety.
- Their excuse was that they feared a turn of fortune, which shows their weak faith.
- Allah will bring victory or His command, and their hidden hypocrisy will be exposed and they will regret it.

53.text:
"Only then, the believers will ask one another, “Are these the ones who swore solemn oaths by Allah that they were with you?” Their deeds have been in vain, so they have become losers"

This verse describes the moment when the hypocrites are exposed. The believers ask one another in amazement whether these are the people who swore great oaths of loyalty to them. The verse ends by saying their deeds were lost.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Only then, the believers will ask one another."** The material explains that the question is asked when the hypocrisy has come out into the open. The believers are amazed at people who had sworn faithfulness and now stand exposed.

**"Are these the ones who swore solemn oaths by Allah that they were with you?"** The material says that the hypocrites swore by Allah, which is the most binding oath, that they were with the believers in faith and support. Their oaths were false, and the believers see the falsehood plainly.

**"Their deeds have been in vain."** The material says that their works were thwarted in this life, since their hypocrisy did them no good. It says their loss is also in the next life, through the punishment prepared for them.

**"So they have become losers."** The material says that they lost their true goal and the reward of the Hereafter. The verse is read as a warning that the outward claim of loyalty means nothing without true faith.

### The lesson of the trial

The material draws a lesson from the verse. Every test in the world is a test of intention. A believer proves his intention by refusing to fear the dangers of the path. The help of Allah comes after that first step. A person who does not take the first step is a transgressor in the sight of Allah, and cannot expect His help. The material says that the Islamic life is one of struggle, and that the believer's mission is to guide others away from the path of hell and towards paradise.

### The hypocrites of Madinah

The material explains that the hypocrites of Madinah, led by Abdullah bin Ubayy and his followers, were the ones who swore loyalty. They had hidden their doubts. When the victory came, first with the conquest of Makkah, and then when the Jews were punished, their claims were exposed. The material says that everyone saw these events within a few days, and that the verse foretold them.

### In short

- The believers wonder at the hypocrites who had sworn their loyalty, once their hypocrisy is exposed.
- Their deeds were wasted in this life and the next, and so they have become losers.
- The lesson is that a believer must prove his intention by standing firm rather than seeking safety in false alliances.

54.text:
"O believers! Whoever among you abandons their faith, Allah will replace them with others who love Him and are loved by Him. They will be humble with the believers but firm towards the disbelievers, struggling in the Way of Allah; fearing no blame from anyone. This is the favour of Allah. He grants it to whoever He wills. And Allah is All-Bountiful, All-Knowing"

This verse speaks to the believers about the danger of apostasy. It says that if some turn away from their faith, Allah will bring a people who love Him and whom He loves. These people are humble towards the believers, firm against the disbelievers, and strive in the way of Allah without fearing the blame of anyone. The verse is both a warning and a promise. It says that the religion does not depend on any one group, and that Allah is able to raise up others.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O believers! Whoever among you abandons their faith."** The material explains that the verse speaks to the Muslims. It warns that turning back from faith is possible, and that such a person has turned away from the religion and from its obligations.

**"Allah will replace them with others who love Him and are loved by Him."** The material says the promise is that Allah brings a people in their place, whom He loves and who love Him. The love is both ways. Al-Hakim, in his collection of sound reports, records that the Prophet ﷺ pointed to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and said that the people will be like him. The material notes that the verse was also read as a prophecy of the apostasy that followed the death of the Prophet ﷺ, and of the people who fought it.

**"Humble with the believers but firm towards the disbelievers."** The material explains that the Arabic word for humble also means easy to deal with and gentle. These people are soft with their brothers in faith and firm against the enemies of Allah. The material says that their love and enmity are for Allah, His Messenger and His religion, and not for their own persons or interests. Al-Basri, Dahhak and Qatadah are reported to have said that the verse was about the first of these people, and the material reads it as applying to others who follow in the same path.

**"Struggling in the Way of Allah, fearing no blame from anyone."** The material explains jihad as the struggle to establish the true faith, which requires both devotion and fervour for the mission. The material says that the leader of a movement faces the force of the adversary and the criticism of his own people. The verse says that these people do not care for blame.

**"This is the favour of Allah. He grants it to whoever He wills."** The material says that these qualities are a gift of Allah, given to those who deserve them.

### The apostasy after the Prophet ﷺ

The material gives a history of the apostasy. Musaylimah al-Kadhdhab claimed prophethood in his lifetime, and the Prophet ﷺ did not live to fight him. Aswad al-Ansi of Yemen made the same claim, and he was killed the day after the Prophet ﷺ died. Tulayhah ibn Khuwaylid of Banu Asad also claimed prophethood. Groups from these tribes turned away during the last illness of the Prophet ﷺ, and after his death seven tribes refused to pay zakah to the caliph.

The material says that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq faced great grief, and that his patience and courage carried the community through. He consulted the Companions, and none of them agreed to war against the rebels at first, since the danger was that foreign powers would invade the new state. Abu Bakr gave a speech that said he would fight anyone who separated prayer from zakah, even alone. The Companions then rallied around him, and the army was organised. Khalid ibn Walid was sent to Yamamah against Musaylimah, who was killed by Wahshi. His followers repented. Khalid later fought against Tulayhah, who fled and later returned to Islam. News of Aswad's death reached Madinah in Rabi al-Awwal, the first victory of the Siddiqi caliphate, and afterwards the Companions won against the tribes that refused zakah.

The material says that the end of the verse was fulfilled in this history, since the party of Allah prevailed. It adds that the qualities named in the verse were present in Abu Bakr and the Companions with him.

### The lesson for every age

The material says the most sound view is that the verse includes Abu Bakr and his companions, and also every believer who confronts disbelief and apostasy until the Last Day. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and others are named in some reports, and the material says these do not contradict the first view.

The material notes that one who has embraced Faith and does not meet its demands has turned away in the sight of Allah. The people of true faith have their whole being filled with faith, so that their relation with Allah is one of love. Their concern for the cause of Islam makes them kind to their brothers, and they never turn their power against them. The verse calls them to a life of struggle, and the material says that such people, when they meet together in numbers, are destined to become dominant in their land.

### Seven counsels and the humble believer

The material records a report from Ahmad, which Abu Dharr gave, that his intimate friend the Prophet ﷺ commanded him to do seven things. He was to love the poor and sit near them. He was to look at those below him and not above him. He was to keep the ties of kinship even when they cut them. He was not to ask anyone for anything. He was to speak the truth even when it was bitter, and to fear no blame for the sake of Allah. He was to say often, there is no power and no strength except with Allah, since these words are a treasure under the Throne. The material also gives a hadith in which the Prophet ﷺ said that the believer should not humiliate himself, and when asked how a person does that, he said by taking on trials he cannot bear. The material says the humble believer is humble in the right way, not in weakness.

The material says that the qualities of the people in the verse are a grace from Allah. Those who have them received them from His bounty. The verse also calls them to be people of the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and to keep their hearts from the fitnah of turning away.

### The strength from Allah

The material links the verse to 58:22, which says that Allah strengthens the believers with a ruh from Himself. It also links the verse to 48:29 of Surah al-Fath, which describes the Companions as firm against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. These qualities of the Companions are a model for every believer who faces the same trial.

### The Khutbah of Abu Bakr

The material records the khutbah of Abu Bakr al-Akbar, called As-Siddiq, after the Prophet ﷺ died. He said that whoever turns back from the injunctions of the Prophet ﷺ and the law of Islam, it is his duty to wage jihad against them. He said that even if all the jinn and humans and all the trees and stones were gathered against him, and he had no comrade to help him, he would stand alone and carry the struggle. The Companions then rose with him and set out the battle plan. The material says that the words of this khutbah opened the hearts of the Companions to jihad against the apostasy.

### In short

- The verse warns that people may turn away from faith, and promises that Allah will bring a people in their place whom He loves.
- These people are gentle with the believers, firm against the disbelievers, and fear no blame in the way of Allah.
- The verse was fulfilled in the wars of apostasy under Abu Bakr, and it applies to every believer who stands firm in the same way.

55.text:
"Your only guardians are Allah, His Messenger, and fellow believers—who establish prayer and pay alms-tax with humility"

This verse sets out who the believers should take as guardians. It names Allah, His Messenger and the believers who establish prayer and pay zakah with humility. It follows the warning against friendship with the Jews and Christians.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Your only guardians are Allah, His Messenger, and fellow believers."** The material explains that the believer's real loyalty is to these three. The Arabic word is walī, which means guardian, ally and friend. The material says that this is the true friendship that a believer owes.

**"Who establish prayer and pay alms-tax with humility."** The material explains that the believers in view establish the five daily prayers and pay zakah, and that they bow in prayer with the Prophet ﷺ in congregation. The verse describes them as humble, since they give their wealth for the needy and bow before Allah.

### The occasion of revelation

The material records that Abdullah bin Salam and his companions were shunned by the Jews after they embraced Islam. Abdullah bin Salam said to the Prophet ﷺ that their people had abandoned them. The verse was revealed in answer. It told them that their guardian is Allah, His Messenger and the believers, and not the Jews.

The material also reads the verse in the light of the Qur'an's call to love the Prophet. It cites the verse on following him, which says that Allah will love those who follow him, as stated in 3:31. The material says that love of Allah grows through following the Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ.

### In short

- The believer's guardians are Allah, His Messenger and the believers.
- The believers meant are those who establish prayer, pay zakah and bow in humility.
- The verse was revealed after Abdullah bin Salam was shunned by the Jews, and it told him that his real allies are the believers.

56.text:
"Whoever allies themselves with Allah, His Messenger, and fellow believers, then it is certainly Allah's party that will prevail"

This verse closes the passage with a promise. Whoever takes Allah, His Messenger and the believers as allies belongs to the party of Allah, and that party will prevail.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Whoever allies themselves with Allah, His Messenger, and fellow believers."** The material explains that this is a call to take the right allies. The alliance is with the three named in the previous verse.

**"Then it is certainly Allah's party that will prevail."** The material explains that the party of Allah is the group that follows His Messenger and the believers. The verse promises that they will be victorious, as the Qur'an promises elsewhere. The material cites 14:19 and 20, which say that if Allah wills, He can replace a people with a new creation, and 48:29, which describes the companions of the Prophet ﷺ as severe towards disbelievers and merciful among themselves.

### The meaning of bowing

The material explains the word for bowing in the verse. Some scholars read it as the bowing position of the prayer, which is a basic pillar of salah. The material says that the verse names prayer and then the bowing, to show that the prayer of the believers is different from the prayer of the Jews and Christians. Others, Abu Hayyan in al-Bahr al-Muhit and al-Zamakhshari in al-Kashshaf, took the word in its lexical sense of bowing in modesty and humility. The material notes that the same view is taken in Tafsir Mazhari.

The material also gives a report that the verse was revealed about Ali. He was in prayer and had bowed in ruku when a needy man asked him for help. Without finishing his bowing, he took a ring from his finger and gave it to the man. The material says that the report shows how quickly a believer may help the needy, and that the verse was revealed about this act. Ali's love for Allah and His Messenger is also cited, in a hadith in which the Prophet ﷺ said that whoever he is a friend to, Ali is also a friend to him.

### In short

- Whoever allies with Allah, His Messenger and the believers belongs to the party of Allah.
- The party of Allah is promised victory, and the material says this was seen in the Companions' wars of apostasy.
- The believer's loyalty is to the faith and its people, not to those who oppose it.

57.text:
"O believers! Do not seek the guardianship of those given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers who have made your faith a mockery and amusement. And be mindful of Allah if you are ˹truly˺ believers"

This verse forbids the believers from taking as close friends the People of the Book and the disbelievers who mock the religion of Islam. It ends with a call to taqwa, the fear of Allah, as the sign of true faith.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O believers!"** The address opens the section with the same warning as 5:51. The material explains that the believers are commanded to keep their own loyalty, and not to seek friendship with those who ridicule their faith.

**"Do not seek the guardianship of those given the Scripture before you."** The material says the People of the Book are named first. Abu Hayyan, in al-Bahr al-Muhit, notes that they were already included among the disbelievers, but they are named separately because they are nearer to Islam than other disbelievers. Few of them embraced Islam, since their pride in their Scripture made them refuse the truth. The mockery of the Muslims was the thing they showed most.

**"And the disbelievers who have made your faith a mockery and amusement."** The material explains that the word for disbelievers here refers to idolaters. Ibn Mas'ud's recitation read it as those who commit shirk. The verse names their conduct as mockery, because they regard the acts of Islam, which bring good in this life and the next, as something to laugh at.

**"And be mindful of Allah if you are truly believers."** The material says that taqwa is the fear of Allah that keeps one from taking enemies as friends. The believer shows that his faith is true by keeping this fear.

### The wider principle

The material cites 22:30, which tells the believers to shun the evil of idols, and it reads the word disbelievers in 5:57 as a clarification of that category. It cites the verse that says believers should not take the disbelievers as friends in place of the believers, and that whoever does so will not be helped by Allah, except when there is a real danger.

The material records that Rifa'ah ibn Zayd and Suwayd ibn al-Harith were among those who showed faith outwardly but were hypocrites, and that Ibn 'Abbas said the verse was revealed about them. Some Muslims used to show them affection, and the verse forbade it. The material also notes that a people who mock sacred things lose the sense of what is right, and the friendship of believers with them is possible only in the course of calling them to the truth.

### In short

- The believers must not take as close friends the People of the Book or the disbelievers who mock Islam.
- The mockery of the Muslims is the thing that marks such people out, and the verse was applied to hypocrites who showed false affection.
- True faith is shown by the fear of Allah that keeps the believer from such friendship.

58.text:
"When you call to prayer, they mock it in amusement. This is because they are a people without understanding"

This verse describes how the disbelievers mock the call to prayer. It says the reason is that they are a people without understanding.

### Phrase by phrase

**"When you call to prayer."** The call is the adhan, which is the greatest of the acts of worship in public. The material says that the adhan is announced to call people to salah, and that for those with sound minds it is a noble act. The iqamah is the second call, made just before the prayer begins. Az-Zuhri said that Allah mentioned the adhan in His Book, in the verse on the call to prayer.

**"They mock it in amusement."** The material explains that the mockery was made in play and jest. The verse describes the people of the Book and the disbelievers, and the material gives the following reports.

The first report is from al-Kalbi, who said that when the Prophet ﷺ appointed a caller to prayer and the Muslims stood to pray, the Jews mocked them, saying that they had stood up and might never stand up, that they had prayed and might never pray. This verse was revealed in reply.

The second report is from al-Suddi, about a man of the helpers in Madinah. Whenever he heard the caller say that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, he said, may the liar be burnt. One night his servant brought a fire into the house, and a spark set the house alight while the family slept, and all of them died in the fire.

The third report concerns the disbelievers who envied the Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims for the call to prayer. They asked why the Prophet ﷺ had invented a cry like the cry of camels, which the earlier prophets did not use. The material says that Allah answered this in 41:33, which says that no one is better in speech than the one who calls to his Lord, does good, and says he is of those who submit.

### The lack of understanding

The material explains that the reason for their mockery was that they do not understand. Qadi Thanaullah of Panipat, in Tafsir Mazhari, is said to have observed that Allah calls them without understanding even though their intelligence in worldly matters is well known. The material cites 30:7, which says that they know the outward matters of the present life and are heedless of the Hereafter. It concludes that a person may be clever in one field and blind in another.

### In short

- The disbelievers mocked the call to prayer, which is an act of worship.
- The verse was revealed in response to Jews who mocked the Muslims, and to disbelievers who envied the adhan.
- The reason for the mockery is that they lack understanding of what matters most, as 30:7 says.

59.text:
"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O People of the Book! Do you resent us only because we believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before—while most of you are rebellious?”"

This verse commands the Prophet ﷺ to ask the People of the Book a question. Do they resent the believers for anything but their faith in Allah, the Qur'an and the earlier books? It says that most of them are rebellious.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Say, O Prophet."** The command is to speak directly to the People of the Book. The material explains that the address is a challenge to them to find fault with the believers, and that they cannot find any fault except faith.

**"Do you resent us only because we believe in Allah."** The material says that the believers accept Allah and His books, and they do not reject the earlier prophets. The verse brings out the sense that their resentment is baseless.

**"And what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before."** The material records a report from Ibn 'Abbas that a group of Jews asked the Prophet ﷺ about the prophets he believed in. He said that he believed in Allah and what was revealed to him, and in what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the tribes, and to Moses and Jesus. He made no distinction between them. When he mentioned Jesus, they rejected his prophethood and said that they knew of no people less fortunate in this world and the next than the Muslims. Allah then revealed this verse. The material cites 2:136 for the statement of the belief of the Prophet ﷺ.

**"While most of you are rebellious."** The material explains that the word most is not all. Some of the People of the Book kept faith and followed the Torah and Injil, and then believed in the Qur'an when it came. The material says that the word most is used to show that many have turned away, and it is connected to the earlier claim that they resent the believers.

### The cause of the resentment

The material cites 85:8 and 9:74 for the same point. In 85:8 the believers are described as those who had no fault but that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy. In 9:74, Allah and His Messenger had enriched them by His bounty, and yet some turned against them. The material gives an agreed hadith in which the Prophet ﷺ asked what caused Ibn Jamil to refuse zakah, when Allah had made him rich after he was poor. The material says the refusal of charity is a sign of the rebellious state.

### In short

- The verse commands the Prophet ﷺ to ask the People of the Book what fault they find in the believers.
- The only thing they can name is faith in Allah and His books, and this is no fault.
- The verse says that most of them are rebellious, and that the believers' faith is a reason for their resentment only in their own hearts.

60.text:
"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Shall I inform you of those who deserve a worse punishment from Allah ˹than the rebellious˺? It is those who earned Allah's condemnation and displeasure—some being reduced to apes and pigs and worshippers of false gods. These are far worse in rank and farther astray from the Right Way.”"

This verse continues the speech to the People of the Book. It asks whether they want to be told of those who deserve a worse punishment. It describes those who earned Allah's condemnation, some of whom were transformed into apes and pigs, and those who worshipped false gods.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Shall I inform you of those who deserve a worse punishment from Allah?"** The material explains that the question is put in the form of a comparison. The Qur'an speaks in this gentle way to avoid direct blame, and the material describes it as a principle of calling people to the truth, that one should not make addressees angry.

**"Those who earned Allah's condemnation and displeasure."** The material says that the curse of Allah means being cast out of His mercy, and His wrath means the anger after which He will not be pleased with them. The material notes that this describes the people who rejected the call of the prophets.

**"Some being reduced to apes and pigs."** The material notes that this transformation is mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah and again in Surat Al-A'raf. Ibn Mas'ud reported that the Prophet ﷺ was asked whether the monkeys and pigs of the present day were those who had been transformed. He said that Allah never destroyed a people by transforming them and giving them offspring, and that the monkeys and pigs existed before. Muslim recorded it.

**"And worshippers of false gods."** The Arabic word taghut refers to anything that is worshipped besides Allah with its consent. The material says those who worshipped such beings and served them became their servants.

**"These are far worse in rank and farther astray from the Right Way."** The material explains that the word far worse does not mean that the believers are less astray, but that these people are very far astray. The material ends with a description of the true believers, who enjoy the best abode in Paradise.

### The rebuke of the People of the Book

The material reads the verse as a rebuke to the People of the Book, who mocked the religion of Allah, which is the oneness of Allah and worship of Him alone. How could they mock the believers while they had these same characteristics? The verse is a reminder that their own history includes curse and transformation, and that the worship of false gods is a deeper error than anything the believers do.

### In short

- The verse asks the People of the Book whether they want to be told of those who deserve a worse punishment than the rebellious.
- It names those who earned the curse of Allah, some of whom were transformed into apes and pigs, and those who worshipped taghut.
- These people are farther astray than the believers, and the People of the Book who mock the believers share this condition.

61.text:
"When they come to you ˹believers˺ they say, “We believe.” But they are committed to disbelief when they enter and when they leave. And Allah knows what they hide"

This verse describes hypocrites who come to the believers and say they believe, while they enter and leave in disbelief. Allah knows what they hide in their hearts.

### Phrase by phrase

**"When they come to you they say, 'We believe.'"** The material explains that these people claimed faith in words, when they came to the believers. The verse describes the hypocrites of Madinah, who were impressed by Islam and did not want to face its open enmity.

**"But they are committed to disbelief when they enter and when they leave."** The material says their hearts were steady in the religion of their fathers, and they only made a show of belief. They entered with disbelief and left with it. The material says they did not benefit from the knowledge they heard from the Prophet ﷺ, and that his advice did not move them.

**"And Allah knows what they hide."** The material explains that Allah knows the secrets of the heart, even when the hypocrites pretend otherwise to His creatures. The material says that they forget that their dealings are with God, and that God deals with them based on the reality and not on their words.

### The rabbis and the scholars

The material records that some Jews of Madinah were impressed by Islam, and that the leading rabbis and the scholars of the Torah were busy with the work of religion, living on what their position brought them. The verse concerns those who showed belief while their hearts remained with their old religion, for the sake of their worldly position. The material says that Allah knows this, and that it is folly to think that a show of faith can deceive Him.

### In short

- The hypocrites claim belief when they come to the believers, but they enter and leave with disbelief in their hearts.
- They do not benefit from the knowledge they hear, because their hearts are closed.
- Allah knows what they hide, and they cannot deceive Him by a show of faith.

62.text:
"You see many of them racing towards sin, transgression, and consumption of forbidden gain. Evil indeed are their actions"

This verse describes the eagerness of many of the People of the Book for sin, transgression and forbidden gain. It calls their conduct evil.

### Phrase by phrase

**"You see many of them racing towards sin."** The material explains that the word many is used to exclude the good ones among them. The word racing shows how habitual their sin had become. The material says a bad deed repeated becomes a fixed habit, so that it is done almost without thought. The same expression is used of the believers in 3:114, who race towards good deeds.

**"Transgression, and consumption of forbidden gain."** The material explains that aggression and the eating of the unlawful are sins, but they are named separately to stress the ruin they bring. The material says the Jews were guilty of unjustly taking the wealth of people through bribes and riba.

**"Evil indeed are their actions."** The material says this is a judgement on their conduct. It calls their deeds evil and horrible, because of the wrong they committed.

### In short

- Many of the People of the Book were eager for sin, transgression and forbidden gain.
- The word racing shows that these evils had become a fixed habit.
- Their deeds are judged evil, and the verse names bribery and riba as examples of the forbidden gain.

63.text:
"Why do their rabbis and scholars not forbid them from saying what is sinful and consuming what is unlawful? Evil indeed is their inaction"

This verse rebukes the rabbis and scholars for failing to forbid the people from sin and from unlawful gain. It calls their silence evil.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Why do their rabbis and scholars not forbid them?"** The material explains the two names. The Rabbaniyyun are the people of Allah, the scholars in positions of authority. The Ahbar are the scholars of the Torah. The question is one of rebuke, for the leaders were expected to stop the people from wrongdoing.

**"From saying what is sinful and consuming what is unlawful."** The material says that the sin is the lying, false testimony, and the wrongful consumption of wealth. The leaders were guilty because they did not forbid these acts.

**"Evil indeed is their inaction."** The material says the verse ties the duty of forbidding evil to the leaders, as Al-Bahr al-Muhit and Ibn Jarir both note. Ali ibn Abi Talib said in a speech that those before them the earlier nations fell into ruin after their sins went unopposed by their scholars. When they persisted, they were overtaken by punishment. Ibn 'Abbas said that no verse of the Qur'an contains a more severe warning than this one.

### The duty of forbidding evil

The material gives a hadith from Jarir, which Ahmad recorded. The Prophet ﷺ said that there is no people among whom there are those who commit sins, while the others are stronger and do not stop them, except that Allah will send a punishment on them. Abu Dawud recorded a version in which the Prophet ﷺ said that whoever lives among people committing evil, and does not stop them when he is able to, will be punished by Allah before he dies. Ibn Majah also recorded it.

The material says the duty of enjoining the right and forbidding the wrong is a unique distinction of the Muslim community, and that the Muslims kept their excellence while they held to this duty. When they left it to the state alone, their families and children turned away from the Shari'ah. Ibn Abi Hatim recorded this. The material gives an account from Malik ibn Dinar, that Allah asked the angels to destroy a town where a devout servant lived, because he had never shown anger at sins. The material also gives the example of Yusha ibn Nun, whose story is told in Ibn Jarir's collection, to whom Allah revealed that a hundred thousand of his people would be destroyed, forty thousand of them righteous, because the righteous had eaten and drunk with the wicked and never frowned on their sins.

### In short

- The rabbis and scholars were rebuked for not forbidding the people from lying, false testimony and wrongful gain.
- Ali and Ibn 'Abbas both cited this verse as a severe warning, and Ibn Jarir recorded Ibn 'Abbas's words, and the Prophet ﷺ taught that sins not stopped bring a punishment on all.
- The duty of forbidding wrong is a mark of the Muslim community, and its neglect brings the same ruin the verse describes.

64.text:
"˹Some among˺ the Jews said, “Allah is tight-fisted.” May their fists be tied and they be condemned for what they said. Rather, He is open-handed, giving freely as He pleases. That which has been revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ from your Lord will only cause many of them to increase in wickedness and disbelief. We have stirred among them hostility and hatred until the Day of Judgment. Whenever they kindle the fire of war, Allah puts it out. And they strive to spread corruption in the land. And Allah does not like corruptors"

This verse answers a slander of some Jews, who said that Allah is tight-fisted. It shows that the words are a curse on the speakers, that Allah's hands are open and His giving is full, and that the revelation increases the hostility of the disbelievers. The verse ends by saying that Allah does not love those who spread corruption.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Some among the Jews said, 'Allah is tight-fisted.'"** The material explains that the speakers meant that Allah is a miser who does not spend what He has. The verse says this is a slander. Ibn 'Abbas explained that they did not mean His hand was literally tied, but that He was stingy. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, As-Suddi and Ad-Dahhak gave the same meaning. The material cites 17:29, which forbids the believer to be tied in stinginess or to stretch the hand out in extravagance. Ikrimah said the verse was revealed about Finhas, one of the Jews, who said that Allah is poor and they are rich. Abu Bakr struck him for it.

**"May their fists be tied and they be condemned for what they said."** The material says the curse is the answer to their slander. The Jews are stingy, envious and cowardly, and their humiliation is the fulfilment of the curse. The material cites 3:112, which says that disgrace is put over them.

**"Rather, He is open-handed, giving freely as He pleases."** The material explains that both hands of Allah are outstretched, and that He spends as He wills. Abu Hurayrah narrated a hadith that the right hand of Allah is full and that no spending decreases what He has. The hadith is recorded in the two sahihs.

**"That which has been revealed to you will only cause many of them to increase in wickedness and disbelief."** The material says that the revelation brings blessing to the believers and a calamity to their enemies. It increases the believers in faith and good works, and increases the disbelievers in envy and in denial. The material cites 41:44, which says the Qur'an is guidance and healing for those who believe, and 17:82, which says the Qur'an increases the wrongdoers in nothing but loss.

**"We have stirred among them hostility and hatred until the Day of Judgment."** The material explains that their groups and sects will never be united, because they have not agreed on the truth and have opposed the Prophet ﷺ.

**"Whenever they kindle the fire of war, Allah puts it out."** The material says that every plot they make against the Prophet ﷺ is extinguished by Allah, and their evil returns to harm them. The material reads this as Allah keeping their designs in check through divisions among them.

**"And they strive to spread corruption in the land. And Allah does not like corruptors."** The material says it is their habit to cause mischief on earth. Allah does not love those who do so.

### The Jews of Madinah

The material gives the background of the verse. The Jews of Madinah had wealth and influence, and when the Prophet ﷺ came they remained unmoved, because they wanted to keep their power and the offerings they received. They turned against the call of truth, and as a punishment their wealth was reduced. In their frustration they spoke these words. The material says the reports on this came from the Lubab, transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, which Al-Tabarani and Abu al-Shaykh recorded.

### In short

- Some Jews slandered Allah by calling Him tight-fisted, and the verse answers with a curse on them and a description of His open hands.
- The revelation brings blessing to the believers and an increase in envy and denial for the disbelievers.
- Allah does not love those who spread corruption in the land.

65.text:
"Had the People of the Book only been faithful and mindful ˹of Allah˺, We would have certainly absolved them of their sins and admitted them into the Gardens of Bliss"

This verse gives the promise that faith and taqwa would bring forgiveness and Paradise to the People of the Book.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Had the People of the Book only been faithful and mindful of Allah."** The material explains that the People of the Book are the Jews and Christians. The verse says that faith and taqwa are the way to their salvation. The material notes that the Qur'an calls them to faith in the Prophet ﷺ, and that their refusal is the cause of their loss.

**"We would have certainly absolved them of their sins."** The material says that the expiation of sins is the forgiveness of Allah. It would have removed the dangers they faced and granted them their goals.

**"And admitted them into the Gardens of Bliss."** The material says this is the reward of Paradise for those who believe and fear Allah. The material notes that the promise in this verse is about the Hereafter, and that the next verse adds a promise for this world.

### In short

- Faith and taqwa would have brought the People of the Book forgiveness of their sins and entry into Paradise.
- The promise is for the Hereafter, and the material notes that the next verse extends it to this life.
- The refusal of the People of the Book was the cause of their loss.

66.text:
"And had they observed the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to them from their Lord, they would have been overwhelmed with provisions from above and below. Some among them are upright, yet many do nothing but evil"

This verse promises that if the People of the Book had kept the Torah, the Gospel and the revelation sent to them, they would have been given provision from above and below. It then says that some of them are upright, but many do evil.

### Phrase by phrase

**"And had they observed the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to them from their Lord."** The material says the Torah and the Injil were the guidance of the earlier prophets, and that they testify to the truth of the Prophet ﷺ. The verse calls on the People of the Book to follow them and not to alter them.

**"They would have been overwhelmed with provisions from above and below."** The material explains that provision from above and below means ample and constant sustenance. The material cites 7:96, which says that if the people of the towns had believed and feared Allah, He would have opened blessings from heaven and earth. It also cites 7:159, which speaks of a community among the people of Musa who guided others by truth and established justice.

**"Some among them are upright."** The material says some of the People of the Book were moderate and on the right path. They were the ones who first held to the Torah and Injil, and then believed in the Qur'an and the Prophet ﷺ. The material cites 57:27, which says that Allah gave the reward to those among the followers of Isa who believed.

**"Yet many do nothing but evil."** The material says the majority were evil in their conduct. The verse is not a judgement on all of them, but on most.

### The promise and the grade of the middle course

The material explains that this promise is not a rule that sustenance always follows faith, but a promise made to a particular group under particular conditions.
