Some believers in the time of the Prophet ﷺ received it in full, such as the Negus, the king of Abyssinia, and Abdullah ibn Salam. The material says that the general rule is that the pure life is promised to the believers, and it may come as abundance or as outward hardship, as it did with the prophets and the righteous.

The material cites 35:32-33, which speaks of three classes of the people of the Book: those who wrong themselves, those who follow a middle course, and those who are foremost in good deeds. The middle course is given to this community, and the foremost are above it.

### In short

- The verse promises that the People of the Book would have had ample provision if they had kept the Torah, the Gospel and the revelation.
- Some of them are upright, and the material cites 7:159 and 57:27 for those who believed.
- The verse does not make a general rule, but it describes a promise to a particular group, and it cites 35:32-33 for the three classes.

67.text:
"O Messenger! Convey everything revealed to you from your Lord. If you do not, then you have not delivered His message. Allah will ˹certainly˺ protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the people who disbelieve"

This verse commands the Prophet ﷺ to convey all that has been revealed to him, and it warns that failing to convey even part of it would mean he had not delivered the message at all. It then promises that Allah will protect him from the people, and it ends by saying that Allah does not guide the disbelievers.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O Messenger! Convey everything revealed to you from your Lord."** The material explains that the address uses the title Messenger. The command is to convey the whole of the revelation, without withholding any part. The material notes that the Prophet ﷺ fulfilled this command in the best way. Aisha is reported to have said that whoever says Muhammad hid any part of the revelation is lying, and Al-Bukhari recorded this report.

**"If you do not, then you have not delivered His message."** The material says that to hide even one verse would mean that the message was not delivered. Ibn 'Abbas explained that if the Prophet ﷺ hid only one verse revealed to him, then he had not conveyed the message of his Lord. The material says the Prophet ﷺ knew the gravity of this, and it notes that Az-Zuhri said the message comes from Allah, the Messenger is its deliverer, and the believers' duty is to submit to it.

**"Allah will certainly protect you from the people."** The material explains that Allah's protection means He will aid and support the Prophet ﷺ and give him victory over his enemies. The verse removes his fear and grief, because none of them can touch him with harm.

**"Indeed, Allah does not guide the people who disbelieve."** The material explains that the Prophet's task is to convey, and that guidance belongs to Allah, who guides whom He wills. The material cites 2:272, which says that the guidance of the people is not upon the Prophet, and 13:40, which says that his duty is only to convey, and the reckoning is with Allah.

### The protection before the verse

The material gives reports that the Prophet ﷺ was guarded before this verse was revealed. Aisha reported that on one night the Prophet ﷺ wished that a pious man of his companions would guard him. They heard the sound of arms, and Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas came to guard him. The Prophet ﷺ slept after that. This is recorded in the two sahihs. Another report says this happened in Madinah, after the hijrah and after the marriage of Aisha. Ibn Abi Hatim recorded that the Prophet ﷺ was guarded until this verse was revealed, and then he came out and said to the people that they should leave, since Allah would protect him. At-Tirmidhi recorded it, and Ibn Jarir and Al-Hakim recorded it too. The material gives a report from al-Hasan, in which the Prophet ﷺ said that the charge of conveying the message frightened him, because the people would reject and oppose him, but that when this verse came, he was at peace.

### The farewell sermon

The material explains that the Prophet ﷺ fulfilled the command at the farewell hajj. He addressed a great gathering of his Companions, and asked them whether he had conveyed the message. They said that he had, and that he had fulfilled the trust and given sincere advice. He raised his finger toward the sky and then toward them and said, O Allah, did I convey? Jabir bin Abdullah reported this in Muslim's collection. The material says that those present were to convey the message to those who were absent, including those yet to be born. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Mu'adh are also reported to have passed on what they had heard before their deaths, so that they would not carry the trust unfulfilled.

The material notes that the sermon was the constitution of Islam and the last will of the Prophet ﷺ, and that it was given before the Companions at the hajj.

### The lesson for the preacher

The material explains the position of the preacher of the truth. In Arabia the call to pure religion threatened the position of those who held religious authority, and the Prophet ﷺ met the worst opposition. The preacher has two ways open to him. He can take the worldly consequences into account, in which case the work of conveying God's word becomes impossible. Or he can disregard those consequences and trust in God, who promises to help those who devote themselves to preaching. The reaction of the people is natural, but it has a limit set by God's law of trial. The opponents cannot stop the work or prevent its completion, and the acceptance of the message is the responsibility of the hearers.

### In short

- The Prophet ﷺ was commanded to convey the whole of the revelation, and to hide even one part would mean he had not delivered the message.
- Allah promised to protect him from the people, and the guarding stopped after this verse came.
- The farewell sermon shows the Prophet ﷺ fulfilling the command, and the believers are asked to carry the message to those who are absent.

68.text:
"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O People of the Book! You have nothing to stand on unless you observe the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to you from your Lord.” And your Lord's revelation to you ˹O Prophet˺ will only cause many of them to increase in wickedness and disbelief. So do not grieve for the people who disbelieve"

This verse tells the People of the Book that they have no real footing with God unless they keep the Torah, the Gospel and what has been revealed to the Prophet ﷺ from his Lord. It then warns the Prophet ﷺ that the revelation will increase the wickedness of many of them, and tells him not to grieve over them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"You have nothing to stand on unless you observe the Torah, the Gospel."** The material explains that the phrase means that there is no true religion for them unless they act on their books. The Torah and the Injil command the people to follow the Prophet ﷺ and believe in his prophecy, and so keeping them means following him.

**"And what has been revealed to you from your Lord."** The material notes that the verse does not simply name the Qur'an, but speaks of what has been revealed to the Prophet ﷺ. The Companions and the Successors read this as the Qur'an, which was sent to the whole community of the faith, including the Jews and Christians. The material also reads the wording as covering the other revelation the Prophet ﷺ received, which is the explanation of the Qur'an. A hadith recorded by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah says that the Prophet ﷺ was given the Qur'an and something like it, and that a man will one day say the Qur'an is enough, and will take as halal only what the Qur'an calls halal and as haram only what it calls haram, though what the Messenger declares haram is like what Allah declares haram.

**"Will only cause many of them to increase in wickedness and disbelief."** The material explains that the revelation is a blessing for the believers, and for the disbelievers it increases their envy and denial. The Prophet ﷺ is told not to be sad at this.

**"So do not grieve for the people who disbelieve."** The material says this is a comfort to the Prophet ﷺ and the believers. Their disbelief is not their fault and does not reduce his mission.

### Three kinds of rulings

The material explains that the rulings of the Prophet ﷺ come in three kinds. The first are those stated in the Qur'an. The second are those revealed to him through a separate revelation that is not recited. The third are those he gave by ijtihad and qiyas, when no revelation came against them. All three are binding, and they are all included in what has been revealed to him. The material says that the rulings of the earlier books were replaced in part by the later ones, so following the replacing ruling is itself obedience to both books.

### The lesson on the path

The material draws a lesson for the believers. No lineage, no intellect, no spiritual exertion and no inner illumination can bring salvation without adherence to the Shari'ah. The spiritual paths and the discipline of the heart are of no benefit unless they stand within the law of Allah.

### In short

- The People of the Book have no true footing unless they keep the Torah, the Gospel and the revelation to the Prophet ﷺ.
- The revelation is a blessing that increases the faith of the believers and the envy of the disbelievers.
- The Prophet ﷺ is told not to grieve over those who reject the message.

69.text:
"Indeed, the believers, Jews, Sabians and Christians—whoever ˹truly˺ believes in Allah and the Last Day and does good, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve"

This verse names four communities and promises that whoever among them truly believes in Allah and the Last Day and does good will have no fear and no grief. The material reads the promise as one that depends on faith in the Prophet ﷺ and his law, not on the name of the community.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, the believers, Jews, Sabians and Christians."** The material explains that the believers are the Muslims. The Jews are those who were given the Torah. The Christians are those who were given the Injil. The Sabians are a sect that is hard to identify. The material reports from Mujahid that they were a sect of Christians and Magians with no fixed religion, and from Qatadah that they worshipped angels, prayed facing away from the qiblah, and recited the Zabur of Dawud. The material notes that the four Scriptures named in the Qur'an are the Torah, the Zabur, the Injil and the Qur'an, and that the four communities are linked to these books.

**"Whoever truly believes in Allah and the Last Day and does good."** The material says the three parts of faith are belief in Allah, belief in the Last Day, and righteous deeds. The verse does not list every article of faith, since it is not the place to do so. It points to the basic beliefs and invites people to the rest.

**"There will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve."** The material says that whoever takes to obedience, faith and good deeds, whatever he was before, will be acceptable to Allah. The sins and shortcomings of the past are forgiven, and in the Hereafter there is no fear or grief.

### The belief in the Messenger

The material explains that the verse does not mention belief in the Prophet ﷺ, but this does not mean it is not required. It cites 2:285, which says that the believers have faith in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers, and that they make no difference between the messengers. It cites 4:150–151, which condemns those who say they believe in some messengers and reject others. The material reports the saying of the Prophet ﷺ that if Musa were alive, he would have had no choice but to follow him.

The material also argues that the earlier verse about the Companions shows that true belief in Allah includes belief in the messenger. It cites 2:137, which says that if people believe in the same as the prophets believe in, they are on the right path. The material says that the faith of the Companions had belief in the Messenger as a great pillar, and so belief in Allah includes belief in him.

The material says that if any religion were enough for salvation without the Prophet ﷺ, then the sending of the last prophet and the Qur'an would have been unnecessary. It also argues that the Prophet ﷺ fought against the Jews and Christians who rejected him, which would be unjustified otherwise. It cites 38:79, in which Iblis confirms his faith in the Last Day, and asks why he is cursed if belief in Allah and the Last Day were sufficient. The material says the error comes from thinking religion can be given as a gift, and that relations with non-Muslims should be based on tolerance, mercy and justice, while the limits of the religion are kept.

### The earlier verse of 2:62

The material cites 2:62, which has almost the same words. The only difference is that the place of certain words is changed. The message is the same in both places, and it shows that the promise is open to every one of these communities if they believe and do good.

### In short

- Four communities are named, and the promise is open to whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day and does good.
- True faith includes belief in the Prophet ﷺ, as 2:285, 4:150–151 and 2:137 show.
- Anyone who turns to the faith, whatever he was before, has no fear and no grief in the Hereafter.

70.text:
"Indeed, We took a covenant from the Children of Israel and sent them messengers. Whenever a messenger came to them with what they did not desire, they denied some and killed others"

This verse recalls the covenant that God made with the Children of Israel and the way they dealt with the messengers who came to them. Whenever a messenger brought what did not suit their desires, they denied some and killed others.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Indeed, We took a covenant from the Children of Israel and sent them messengers."** The material explains that the covenant was the pledge to believe in God and in His messengers and to act rightly. God sent prophets to them as a continuing mercy, and each one called them back to that pledge.

**"Whenever a messenger came to them with what they did not desire."** The material says this means any message that did not agree with their wishes or their religion as they had shaped it. The verse describes a habit. They accepted what suited them and rejected what did not.

**"They denied some and killed others."** The material gives the examples of Zechariah and Yahya, whom the material names as killed by them. It says that the present tense used for killing is a way of describing past events as if they were happening now, so that the verse keeps its rhythm.

### The history of the covenant

The material gives an account of their history. They broke the pledge again and again, and the people who were punished were the ones who had turned away. It says that after a period of humiliation under the king of Babylon in 586 BC, they were freed under Cyrus in 539 BC, and returned to Jerusalem, and repented. Then they went back to their old ways, and they killed Zechariah and Yahya and planned to kill Isa. The material says the verse is a warning that the same pattern can repeat.

### In short

- God made a covenant with the Children of Israel and sent them messengers to remind them of it.
- They rejected messengers whose message did not suit them, and some were denied and some were killed.
- The verse is a warning that disregard of the covenant brings its own result.

71.text:
"They thought there would be no consequences, so they turned a blind eye and a deaf ear. Yet Allah turned to them in forgiveness ˹after their repentance˺, but again many became blind and deaf. And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do"

This verse describes how they assumed there would be no consequences for what they did, and so became blind and deaf to the truth. It then says that God turned to them in forgiveness after they repented, and that many of them became blind and deaf again.

### Phrase by phrase

**"They thought there would be no consequences."** The material says they believed no harm would come to them for denying and killing the messengers. The phrase can be read as a trial or punishment that would fall on them. The material reads it as a belief that the punishment would never come.

**"So they turned a blind eye and a deaf ear."** The material explains that the blindness and deafness are a state of the heart. They did not see the guidance or hear the truth that was in their hearts, so they were unable to follow it.

**"Yet Allah turned to them in forgiveness after their repentance."** The material says God accepted their repentance after they had returned from their error, and forgave them.

**"But again many became blind and deaf."** The material explains that many of them returned to the same condition after they were forgiven, and died in it. The verse does not say all of them.

**"And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do."** The material says God knows their denials and their killings, and will repay them for them.

### In short

- They assumed no consequences would follow, and they became blind and deaf to the truth.
- God forgave them when they repented, but many of them fell back into the same state.
- God sees all that they do.

72.text:
"Those who say, “Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary,” have certainly fallen into disbelief. The Messiah ˹himself˺ said, “O Children of Israel! Worship Allah—my Lord and your Lord.” Whoever associates others with Allah ˹in worship˺ will surely be forbidden Paradise by Allah. Their home will be the Fire. And the wrongdoers will have no helpers"

This verse declares those who say that Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary, to be in disbelief. It recalls that the Messiah himself told the Children of Israel to worship Allah alone, and it says that whoever associates others with Allah will be forbidden Paradise.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Those who say, Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary, have certainly fallen into disbelief."** The material explains that this is the claim of those who attributed divinity to Isa. It is a claim about Allah that is far beyond what Isa himself taught.

**"The Messiah himself said, O Children of Israel! Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord."** The material explains that Isa called his people to worship Allah alone. The material cites 19:30, where Isa says that he is a servant of Allah who has given him the Scripture and made him a prophet, and 19:36, where he says that Allah is his Lord and theirs, and that they should worship Him.

**"Whoever associates others with Allah will surely be forbidden Paradise."** The material says that association in worship is the one sin that Allah does not forgive, as the verse 4:48 says. Whoever dies in that state will have Paradise forbidden to him and the Fire as his home.

**"And the wrongdoers will have no helpers."** The material says that no one can save them from the state they will be in.

### Isa as servant and the mother of Isa

The material says that Isa was like the earlier prophets, a servant of Allah and a messenger. It cites 43:59, which describes him as only a servant on whom Allah bestowed favour and whom He made an example for the Children of Israel. The material says the first words Isa spoke in the cradle were that he is the servant of Allah. It also reports that the Prophet ﷺ had someone announce to the people that only a believing soul would enter Paradise.

### In short

- Those who claim that Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary, have fallen into disbelief.
- Isa told his people to worship Allah alone, and he called himself a servant.
- Association in worship is the sin that leads to Paradise being forbidden, and the wrongdoers have no helpers.

73.text:
"Those who say, “Allah is one in a Trinity,” have certainly fallen into disbelief. There is only One God. If they do not stop saying this, those who disbelieve among them will be afflicted with a painful punishment"

This verse declares that those who say Allah is one of three in a Trinity have fallen into disbelief. It affirms that there is only One God, and warns that if they do not stop, a painful punishment will fall on those who disbelieve among them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Those who say, Allah is one in a Trinity, have certainly fallen into disbelief."** The material explains that the claim is the belief in God as one of three, with Isa and his mother named as gods alongside Allah. Mujahid said that the verse was revealed about the Christians in particular, and As-Suddi said that it was about taking Isa and his mother as gods. The material cites 5:116, where Allah asks Isa whether he told the people to take him and his mother as two gods besides Allah, and he says that Allah is far beyond that.

**"There is only One God."** The material says this is a plain statement of tawhid. There are not many worthy of worship, and He has no partner.

**"If they do not stop saying this, those who disbelieve among them will be afflicted with a painful punishment."** The material says the warning is a threat of a painful torment in the Hereafter. The verse gives them the chance to stop.

### In short

- Those who say that Allah is one of a Trinity have fallen into disbelief.
- There is only One God, with no partner.
- The warning is that a painful punishment will come if they do not stop.

74.text:
"Will they not turn to Allah in repentance and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful"

This verse calls them back to repentance and forgiveness. It asks them why they do not turn to Allah and seek His forgiveness, and it reminds them that He is All-Forgiving and Most Merciful.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Will they not turn to Allah in repentance and seek His forgiveness?"** The material explains that the question is a rebuke for what they say about Isa. The way back is to repent and ask for forgiveness for the claim that they have made.

**"And Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful."** The material says that Allah forgives the one who repents, and is merciful to him.

### In short

- The verse is a call to repent and ask for forgiveness.
- The rebuke is a question, and the answer is that Allah forgives those who repent.
- The mercy of Allah is open to those who turn back to Him.

75.text:
"The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger. ˹Many˺ messengers had ˹come and˺ gone before him. His mother was a woman of truth. They both ate food. See how We make the signs clear to them, yet see how they are deluded ˹from the truth˺"

This verse says that the Messiah, son of Mary, was only a messenger like those before him. It notes that his mother was a woman of truth, and that both of them ate food, which shows that they were human. It ends by saying that the signs are made clear, yet people turn away from them.

### Phrase by phrase

**"The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger. Many messengers had come and gone before him."** The material explains that the prophets came and passed away, and that Isa likewise passed away. This shows that he was not eternal, which is the mark of divinity.

**"His mother was a woman of truth."** The material says the word here is siddiqah, meaning a woman of complete truthfulness and faith. The material notes that this is a rank of sainthood and not of prophethood, since the Qur'an does not use the word nabiyyah for her. It cites 12:109, which says that messengers were only men sent from among the people of the towns.

**"They both ate food."** The material says that eating shows dependence. A being that needs food depends on the whole chain of causes, and so cannot be God. The material says that not eating would not prove divinity either, since that would make the angels gods.

**"See how We make the signs clear to them, yet see how they are deluded from the truth."** The material says that the signs have been explained clearly, and yet they turn away from them, which is a wonder.

### The reasoning of the verse

The material says that the verse answers the claim of Isa's divinity with three points: he had a beginning, he passed away like the messengers before him, and he depended on food like every human being. These are plain signs, and the verse asks the reader to consider how they still turn away.

### In short

- The Messiah was only a messenger, and the messengers before him passed away.
- His mother was a woman of complete truth, and neither of them was a god, since both ate food.
- The signs are made clear, and it is strange that people still turn away.

76.text:
"Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “How can you worship besides Allah those who can neither harm nor benefit you? And Allah ˹alone˺ is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing.”"

This verse tells the Prophet ﷺ to ask them how they can worship what cannot harm or benefit them, while Allah alone hears and knows all things.

### Phrase by phrase

**"How can you worship besides Allah those who can neither harm nor benefit you?"** The material explains that the question is a rebuke. The idols and the deified persons cannot prevent harm or bring benefit, in this world or the Hereafter.

**"And Allah alone is the All-Hearing, All-Knowing."** The material says that the one who hears their claims about Isa, and knows their state, is Allah alone. The worship is owed only to Him.

### Who is addressed

The material says the verse addresses the people of the Book who attributed godhood to Isa, and in particular the Christians who worshipped him and his mother. It says that the rebuke applies to every worship of what cannot benefit or harm.

### In short

- The question is a rebuke: why worship what cannot harm or benefit you?
- Allah alone hears and knows everything.
- Worship belongs to Him alone.

77.text:
"Say, “O People of the Book! Do not go to extremes in your faith beyond the truth, nor follow the vain desires of those who went astray before ˹you˺. They misled many and strayed from the Right Way.”"

This verse tells the People of the Book not to go to extremes in their faith beyond the truth, and not to follow the desires of earlier people who went astray, misled many, and strayed from the right way.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Do not go to extremes in your faith beyond the truth."** The material explains that the word for extremes means crossing the limits set by religion, in belief or in practice. It names two kinds of extremes that Bani Isra'il fell into. One was excess, by raising prophets to divinity. The other was deficiency, by rejecting them or killing them. The material says the wise path is the middle course.

**"Nor follow the vain desires of those who went astray before you."** The material says that those who went astray before were the forefathers and the earlier teachers, who led many others astray. Following their desires means taking their path instead of the truth.

**"They misled many and strayed from the Right Way."** The material says that the middle path is the right way, and those who left it lost their path.

### The limits of religion

The material explains that religion is a set of limits. It is a crime to fall short of them, and it is equally a crime to go beyond them. Honouring the messengers is also limited. The highest one may go is to regard them as the best of creation. To call them divine or sons of God is excess. The material says the same applies to the reverence of the righteous, and that the Book and the messengers are the two sources of knowledge through which people learn what Allah loves.

The material says that Zamakhshari and others divided extremes into two kinds: the unjust extreme that is forbidden, and a just extreme such as deep and careful study of the faith, which the majority of scholars do not count as excess at all. The material says that study remains within the limits drawn by the Prophet ﷺ, his Companions, and their successors.

### The path of Isra'il in this verse

The material says the verse is addressed to the Children of Israel as well, and warns them not to follow the desires of a people who had gone astray. The verse thus asks for moderation between the two extremes, which is the straight path.

### In short

- The People of the Book are told not to go beyond the truth in their faith.
- Religion is a set of limits, and both excess and deficiency are errors.
- The straight path is the middle course, and the verse warns against following those who strayed before.

78.text:
"The disbelievers among the Children of Israel were condemned in the revelations of David and Jesus, son of Mary. That was for their disobedience and violations"

This verse says that the disbelievers among the Children of Israel were cursed in the revelations given to David and to Jesus, son of Mary. It gives the reason for the curse as their disobedience and their violations.

### Phrase by phrase

**"The disbelievers among the Children of Israel were condemned in the revelations of David and Jesus, son of Mary."** The material explains that the curse was pronounced through the tongues of David and Isa. The material reports that David invoked a curse on them, and they were turned into apes, and that Isa invoked a curse on them, and they were turned into swine. The material notes that Ibn 'Abbas said they were cursed in the Torah, the Injil, the Zabur and the Furqan, which is the Qur'an. The material says the curse began with Musa and ended with the last of the prophets, and the verse names two only because the context requires it.

**"That was for their disobedience and violations."** The material says the disobedience was the breaking of the sabbath and the eating from the table sent from heaven, the killing of prophets, and the making lawful of sin.

### The duty to forbid evil

The material explains that the Children of Israel used not to forbid one another from the evil they committed, and that this was the reason for their curse. The material gives a number of reports from the collections of Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. Hudhayfah bin al-Yaman reported that the Prophet ﷺ said that the believers must enjoin good and forbid evil, or else punishment would come, and their prayers would not be answered. Abu Sa'id al-Khudri reported that the Prophet ﷺ said that whoever sees an evil should change it with his hand, or with his tongue, or with his heart, and that the last is the weakest of faith. Abu Dawud reported that the Prophet ﷺ said that the one who witnesses sin and hates it is like the one who does not witness it. Abu Sa'id also reported that the best jihad is a word of truth spoken before an unjust ruler.

### In short

- David and Isa cursed the disbelievers among the Children of Israel, and the curse was for their disobedience and violations.
- The disbelievers did not forbid one another from evil, which was a central part of their fall.
- The material draws from the hadiths that the duty to speak against evil is a duty for the believers too.

79.text:
"They did not forbid one another from doing evil. Evil indeed was what they did"

This verse says that they did not forbid one another from doing evil, and that what they did was indeed evil.

### Phrase by phrase

**"They did not forbid one another from doing evil."** The material explains that the failure was not only in their own sins, but also in their silence about the sins of others. They allowed evil to continue among them without anyone speaking against it.

**"Evil indeed was what they did."** The material says that the verse is a plain judgement on their conduct. Their silence was as bad as the evil they committed, and God condemned both.

### The lesson of the silence

The material explains that a believer who has faith becomes sensitive to evil. When he sees it, he wants to prevent it, and he keeps his distance from the wrongdoer. When faith weakens, a person cares only for his own interests, and he is neutral about the evils that harm others. The material cites the experience of the Children of Israel as a warning.

### In short

- The people did not forbid one another from evil, and they were condemned for their silence.
- The judgement of the verse is that what they did was evil.
- A believer who loses his concern for others becomes neutral about evil that harms them.

80.text:
"You see many of them taking the disbelievers as allies. Truly wicked are their misdeeds, which have earned them Allah's wrath. And they will be in everlasting torment"

This verse describes the alliances that many of them made with the disbelievers. It says their misdeeds are wicked, that they have earned the wrath of Allah, and that they will be in everlasting torment.

### Phrase by phrase

**"You see many of them taking the disbelievers as allies."** The material explains that the alliances were with the disbelievers of Makkah, and that the material reads the verse as an attack on those who sided with the enemies of the Prophet ﷺ. The material notes that the alliances were made out of spite and hostility to the believers.

**"Truly wicked are their misdeeds, which have earned them Allah's wrath."** The material says that the wrath of Allah is the result of what they have sent forward before themselves, which is their hypocrisy and their support for the disbelievers. The wrath lasts until the Day of Return.

**"And they will be in everlasting torment."** The material says the torment will be on the Day of Resurrection, and that they will remain in it.

### The alliances in the material

The material says that some reports apply the verse to the hypocrites, and that others apply it to the Jews who supported the Quraysh. The material says it is the same act in each case: taking the enemies of the believers as friends.

### In short

- Many of them took the disbelievers as allies, out of spite for the believers.
- Their misdeeds have brought Allah's wrath, and it will remain on them until the Day of Return.
- They will be in everlasting torment.

81.text:
"Had they believed in Allah, the Prophet, and what has been revealed to him, they would have never taken those ˹pagans˺ as allies. But most of them are rebellious"

This verse says that had they truly believed in Allah, His Prophet and what has been revealed to him, they would never have taken the pagans as allies. It then says that most of them are rebellious.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Had they believed in Allah, the Prophet, and what has been revealed to him."** The material explains that true belief includes belief in the Prophet ﷺ and in the Qur'an. A faith that rejects the Prophet ﷺ is not the faith the verse means.

**"They would have never taken those pagans as allies."** The material says that faith in Allah and in the Prophet would have stopped them from taking the enemies of the believers as friends.

**"But most of them are rebellious."** The material says that most of them rebelled against the commands of Allah and His Messenger, and against the signs of His revelation.

### In short

- True belief in Allah and in the Prophet would have stopped them from allying with the pagans.
- Most of them chose rebellion.

82.text:
"You will surely find the most bitter towards the believers to be the Jews and polytheists and the most gracious to be those who call themselves Christian. That is because there are priests and monks among them and because they are not arrogant"

This verse says that the most hostile people towards the believers are the Jews and the polytheists, and that the people nearest to the believers in affection are those who call themselves Christians. It gives the reason as the presence of priests and monks among them, and their lack of arrogance.

### Phrase by phrase

**"You will surely find the most bitter towards the believers to be the Jews and polytheists."** The material explains that the Jews are the most hostile in rebellion, defiance and the opposing of the truth. The material says the Jews killed many of their prophets and tried to kill the Prophet ﷺ several times. It also says that they worked against him, and incited the polytheists to fight him. The material reads the polytheists as the idolators of Makkah.

**"And the most gracious to be those who call themselves Christian."** The material says the praise applies to a particular group of Christians who did not have the hostility of the Jews. The material points to the Christians of Abyssinia, who received the Muslims who migrated there and gave them peace.

**"That is because there are priests and monks among them."** The material explains that the priests and monks are men of knowledge and worship, and that their humility and fairness made them accept the truth. The material cites 57:27, which describes the compassion, mercy and monasticism that God placed in the hearts of the followers of Isa.

**"And because they are not arrogant."** The material says that humility allows a person to listen and to accept the truth. The material contrasts this with the arrogance that the Jews showed.

### The Negus and the delegation

The material explains the cause of the revelation. The Prophet ﷺ advised some of his Companions to migrate to Abyssinia, because its king did not allow anyone to be oppressed in his land. Ja'far ibn Abi Talib led a group, and the Quraysh sent a delegation asking the king to return them. The king heard Ja'far recite about Isa and the Prophet, and he refused to hand them over. When the Muslims later reached Madinah, the Negus sent a delegation of about forty men, with monks among them, to the Prophet ﷺ. They heard the Qur'an, wept, and embraced Islam. The material says that the Negus himself later became a Muslim, and that his son was sent with a letter, though the boat carrying him was lost at sea.

The material cites 3:199, which speaks of the People of the Book who believe in what has been revealed to the Prophet ﷺ and to them, and 28:52-53, which speaks of those given the Scripture who believe in it. It cites 28:55, in which they say they do not seek the ignorant. The material says that the verses describe a group who accepted the truth, and their reward is given in the next verses.

### The limits of this praise

The material says that the praise is not a rule that the Christians are friends of the believers in general, and it cites the view of Abu Bakr al-Jassas that the Christians are closer to shirk in their beliefs. It says that the verse is a difference between the two groups in this one respect, and that the Jews as a group were not God-fearing in the same way.

### In short

- The Jews and the polytheists were the most hostile to the believers, and the Christians who did not share that hostility were the nearest in affection.
- The reason given is the presence of priests and monks who were humble and not arrogant.
- The praise applies to a particular group, as the delegation of the Negus shows, and not to every Christian.

83.text:
"When they listen to what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears for recognizing the truth. They say, “Our Lord! We believe, so count us among the witnesses"

This verse describes a group of people who, on hearing what was revealed to the Messenger, see the truth and weep. They say that they believe and ask to be counted among the witnesses.

### Phrase by phrase

**"When they listen to what has been revealed to the Messenger."** The material explains that the occasion was the recitation before the Negus. Ja'far ibn Abi Talib recited the revelation to the king and his court, and the listeners heard the Qur'an in its plain sense. The material reports that they recognised in it the description of Muhammad ﷺ that was in their own scripture, the Injil.

**"You see their eyes overflowing with tears for recognizing the truth."** The material says the tears were a sign of an inner change. The truth had reached the heart, and the listeners were moved to tears. The material says this was not a matter of words alone, but a turning of the whole being towards the truth.

**"They say, Our Lord! We believe, so count us among the witnesses."** The material explains that they declared belief in Allah, His Book and His Messenger. They asked to be among the witnesses, that is among the community of Muhammad ﷺ who bear witness to the truth.

### The reading of the Qur'an and the heart

The material explains that the words of the Qur'an were a living sign, and that the listeners identified themselves with the truth until they lost their separate identity in it. It says that pride is the main barrier to accepting the truth, and that those who are free of pride are not as strongly opposed to it.

### The Negus and his delegation

The material explains that a group of about forty men came from Abyssinia to Madinah, sent by the Negus. When the Prophet ﷺ recited Surah Ya-Sin to them, they wept and said it was like what had been revealed to Isa. The material cites 57:27, which speaks of the compassion and mercy that God placed in the hearts of the followers of Isa, and 3:199, which describes the People of the Book who humble themselves before Allah. It cites 28:52-53, in which those given the Scripture say they believe in the Qur'an and were Muslims before it, and 28:55, in which they say they do not seek the ignorant. It also cites 27:93, which says that the Prophet ﷺ is told to say that Allah's signs will be shown to them, and they will know them.

### In short

- The listeners recognised the truth in what was recited to them, and their eyes filled with tears.
- They declared their belief and asked to be counted among the witnesses.
- The Negus and his delegation are the historical setting, and the verse describes the inner change that the truth caused.

84.text:
"Why should we not believe in Allah and the truth that has come to us? And we long for our Lord to include us in the company of the righteous.”"

This verse gives their answer to those who blamed them for believing. There is nothing to stop them from believing in Allah and the truth that has come to them, and they long to be included with the righteous.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Why should we not believe in Allah and the truth that has come to us?"** The material explains that this is their answer to the reproaches of the people who opposed them. The truth that had come was the Qur'an and the Messenger, and there was nothing to stop them from believing in it once the conditions for faith were present.

**"And we long for our Lord to include us in the company of the righteous."** The material says that the word for long is a supplement to the word for believe. They hope that Allah will admit them to Paradise among the righteous.

### The reproach against them

The material says that the Jews reproached those who became Muslims. The reply shows that their belief has a clear ground. The material says that this is a model for anyone who turns to the faith and is blamed by his own people. He does not need to justify himself beyond the truth that has come to him.

### In short

- They answered the reproach by saying there was no reason not to believe in Allah and the truth.
- They hoped to be among the righteous in Paradise.
- The reply is a model for anyone who is blamed for accepting the truth.

85.text:
"So Allah will reward them for what they said with Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there forever. And that is the reward of the good-doers"

This verse says that Allah will reward them for what they said with Gardens beneath which rivers flow, where they will remain forever. It calls this the reward of the good-doers.

### Phrase by phrase

**"So Allah will reward them for what they said."** The material explains that the reward is for their declaration of faith, which they made freely from their hearts. The words they spoke were an expression of their whole being.

**"With Gardens under which rivers flow, to stay there forever."** The material describes the Gardens as places of trees and dwellings, with rivers of water, milk, wine and honey. It says they will remain in Paradise for ever, and never leave it.

**"And that is the reward of the good-doers."** The material says the good-doers are those who testify to the Oneness of Allah, and that some reports say the good-doers are those who are kind in speech and deed.

### In short

- Their declaration of faith is rewarded with Gardens beneath which rivers flow.
- They will remain there forever.
- The good-doers are those who testify to the Oneness of Allah and are kind in speech and deed.

86.text:
"As for those who disbelieve and reject Our signs, they will be the residents of the Hellfire"

This verse contrasts the reward of those who believe with the fate of those who disbelieve and reject Allah's signs. They will be the residents of the Hellfire.

### Phrase by phrase

**"As for those who disbelieve and reject Our signs."** The material explains that the disbelief is the rejection of the signs that Allah sent, which are the revelation and the Messenger. The material says that the Jews of the time, and the polytheists, were of this kind, and that their denial was the cause of their loss.

**"They will be the residents of the Hellfire."** The material says that the verse ends with a plain statement that they will remain in the Fire. The material sets this beside the reward of the previous verse, so that the believers and the deniers are shown as two different ends.

### The meaning of the contrast

The material says that the verses from 82 to 86 together show that the people who receive the truth with humility are rewarded, and those who deny it are punished. The contrast is not between two peoples, but between two responses to the same message.

### In short

- The reward of the believers is set against the fate of those who reject the signs of Allah.
- Those who disbelieve and deny the revelation will be the residents of the Fire.
- The contrast is between the people who see the truth and the people who deny it.

87.text:
"O believers! Do not forbid the good things which Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors"

This verse addresses the believers and forbids them to make unlawful the good things that Allah has made lawful for them. It also forbids transgression, and it says that Allah does not love those who transgress.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O believers! Do not forbid the good things which Allah has made lawful for you."** The material explains that the verse was revealed about a group of Companions who wanted to turn away from the world completely. The material names several of them, among them Abu Bakr, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, Salman al-Farisi and Ammar ibn Yasir. They gathered at the house of Uthman ibn Maz'un and agreed to fast by day, pray by night, abstain from meat, fat, perfume and women, and in one report to cut off their male organs. The material reports that they resolved to live as monks.

**"And do not transgress."** The material says that transgression here means making the lawful unlawful without a valid reason. Ibn 'Abbas and others report that the Prophet ﷺ said that he fasts and breaks his fast, prays and sleeps, and marries women, and that whoever turns away from his Sunnah is not of him. The material cites 7:31, which says to eat and drink without wasteful excess, and 25:67, which describes those who are neither extravagant nor miserly.

**"Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors."** The material says the limits are set by Allah, and that the middle way is the path between excess and neglect. Allah does not love those who cross the limits.

### The Sunnah and the rule of the Prophet

The material reports that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said that he had forbidden meat to himself because it stirred his desire. The Prophet ﷺ rebuked the Companions who had made such vows, and the material cites the saying of the Prophet ﷺ, recorded in the two sahihs, that those who are not pleased with his Sunnah are not of him. The material says the Companions had the same question in mind when they asked the wives of the Prophet ﷺ about his worship in private.

### Lawful and unlawful by belief, speech and practice

The material explains that a lawful thing may be made unlawful in three ways. The first is by belief, which is a disbelief if the lawfulness of the thing is proven. The second is by speech, such as an oath that one will never eat a certain food, which must be broken and expiated. The third is by practice, which is permanent abstention from a lawful thing as a means of merit. The material says that such abstention as an act of worship is a bid'ah and a monasticism that is forbidden. Abstention for a real illness or a harm to the body or the heart is not forbidden.

### In short

- The believers are told not to forbid the good things that Allah has made lawful.
- Some Companions wanted to turn to monasticism, and the Prophet ﷺ taught them the Sunnah instead.
- Transgression is crossing the limits of Allah, including making the lawful unlawful as an act of merit.

88.text:
"Eat of the good, lawful things provided to you by Allah. And be mindful of Allah in Whom you believe"

This verse tells the believers to eat of the good and lawful things Allah has provided, and to be mindful of Allah in whom they believe.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Eat of the good, lawful things provided to you by Allah."** The material explains that the words lawful and good are both stated together. The food must be pure, permitted, and of good quality. The material says that the good things are not to be refused as a means of seeking reward.

**"And be mindful of Allah in Whom you believe."** The material explains that taqwa means keeping away from disobedience, and that it is the fear of Allah in all affairs. Refusing the good things as an act of devotion is not taqwa, which is shown by using them as a gift of Allah and giving Him thanks for them.

### The gift and the gratitude

The material says that the verse answers the monastic impulse with the proper attitude to the blessings of Allah. The believer receives them, uses them within their limits, and gives thanks. He does not refuse them as a way of being close to Allah. The material says that the Companions were taught this lesson and that the verse keeps the balance between the two extremes.

### In short

- The believers are to eat the good and lawful food that Allah provides.
- Taqwa is found in using the blessings with gratitude, not in refusing them.
- The verse makes the limits clear, without excess or neglect.

89.text:
"Allah will not call you to account for your thoughtless oaths, but He will hold you accountable for deliberate oaths. The penalty for a broken oath is to feed ten poor people from what you normally feed your own family, or to clothe them, or to free a bondsperson. But if none of this is affordable, then you must fast three days. This is the penalty for breaking your oaths. So be mindful of your oaths. This is how Allah makes things clear to you, so perhaps you will be grateful"

This verse sets out the rule for oaths. Allah does not hold the believers to account for oaths made without intention, but He does hold them to account for deliberate oaths. When a deliberate oath is broken, the expiation is to feed ten poor people, or clothe them, or free a slave, and if none of this can be done, to fast three days.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Allah will not call you to account for your thoughtless oaths, but He will hold you accountable for deliberate oaths."** The material explains that the oath without intention is the word that slips from the tongue, such as saying "no, by Allah" or "yes, by Allah" without meaning it. The material says the same rule was explained in Surah Al-Baqarah, and it cites 2:225, where the accountability for what the hearts have intended is the sin of the Hereafter. The material notes that the accountability in this verse is in this life, through the expiation.

**"The penalty for a broken oath is to feed ten poor people from what you normally feed your own family."** The material says the food should be of the average quality of the household's own meals, given to each poor person at full satisfaction, or in the other reading, one measure of food for each of the ten. Ibn Abbas, Sa'id bin Jubayr and Ikrimah are reported to have read the scale as the average of what one feeds one's family, and Ata' al-Khurasani said it means the best of what one feeds one's family. The material says Ibn Jarir gave the same meaning. The fitrah is the measure used in some of the readings, which is about one and three quarter kilograms of wheat or its value.

**"Or to clothe them."** The material says the clothing must be enough to cover the body, such as a garment for the upper part and another for the lower part. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid are reported to have said that the least is a single garment. The material reports from Abu Malik, Al-Hasan, Ata', Tawus and Ibrahim An-Nakha'i that each of the ten receives one garment.

**"Or to free a bondsperson."** The material gives the report of Umar ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami, who freed a slave girl as an expiation. The Prophet ﷺ asked her where Allah is, and she said above the heavens. He asked who he was, and she said he was the Messenger of Allah. He said to free her, for she is a believer. The report is recorded in Malik's Muwatta, in the Musnad of al-Shafi'i and in the Sahih of Muslim.

**"But if none of this is affordable, then you must fast three days."** The material says that the three expiations are an order of ease, with feeding the easiest and freeing a slave the hardest. It says the choice among them is open, and that the halal and haram of the earlier verses are not made unlawful by an oath. The material reports that Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud read the verse as "three consecutive days," and says that this reading has the force of an explanation from the Companions. Abu Hanifah and some other imams held that the fasts must be consecutive.

**"This is the penalty for breaking your oaths. So be mindful of your oaths."** The material says that the expiation is due only after the oath is broken. An expiation given before the oath is broken is not valid, as there is no prayer before its time and no fast of Ramadan before the month. The verse also tells the believer to guard his oaths, and not to swear casually.

**"This is how Allah makes things clear to you, so perhaps you will be grateful."** The material says that Allah explains His rules so that the believers may give thanks.

### The kinds of oath

The material divides oaths into three kinds. The first is the oath of falsehood, sworn knowingly about a past event that is false. This is a grave sin, and it has no expiation, but it requires repentance and seeking forgiveness. The second is the ineffectual oath, which is sworn by mistake or in the belief that a past event was true when it was not. This brings neither sin nor expiation. The third is the binding oath, sworn about a future act, and it requires expiation when it is broken.

The material explains that the binding oath, which the material calls al-Yamin al-Mun'aqidah, requires the expiation in this verse. The oath of falsehood, Yamin Ghamus, is judged in the Hereafter, and the ineffectual oath, Yamin Laghw, carries no sin. Istighfar, seeking forgiveness, is the remedy for a false oath. It adds that the oath about something lawful should not be made into a vow of abstention, as the earlier verses teach.

### The obligation to keep an oath

The material says that the believer should keep his oaths, and break them only when there is a legal reason or a true need. It says that some scholars held that a person should not swear hastily, and should keep his oath as a thing held in reserve.

### In short

- An oath made without intention is not counted against the believer, but a deliberate oath is.
- The expiation for a broken deliberate oath is feeding ten poor people, clothing them, or freeing a slave, and if none is possible, three days of fasting.
- The expiation is due only after the oath is broken, and the believer should guard his oaths and not swear casually.

90.text:
"O believers! Intoxicants, gambling, idols, and drawing lots for decisions are all evil of Satan’s handiwork. So shun them so you may be successful"

This verse forbids intoxicants, gambling, the idols and the drawing of lots by arrows, and calls them all an evil of Satan's handiwork. It ends by urging the believers to shun them so that they may be successful.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O believers! Intoxicants, gambling, idols, and drawing lots for decisions."** The material explains the four things named in the verse. The material says that the word for the altar stones, ansab, refers to the stones and idols set up for worship. The word azlam refers to the arrows used for lots, and Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata' and Sa'id bin Jubayr are reported to have said that the arrows were for drawing lots. The material says that the word for gambling, maysir, covers the games of chance, and Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ibn Umar are reported to have said that even chess belongs to it.

**"Are all evil of Satan's handiwork."** The material says that the word rijs means filth, something foul to the human taste. Sa'id bin Jubayr said it means sin, and Zayd bin Aslam said it means an evil work of Satan. The verse places these four things in one category, and the material notes that the same words appear in 2:219.

**"So shun them so you may be successful."** The material says that the call to avoid these things is a promise of success in this world and the next. Ibn Majah reports the saying of the Prophet ﷺ that the one who drinks is like the one who worships idols.

### The stages of the prohibition

The material gives the history of the prohibition in several stages. When the Prophet ﷺ migrated to Madinah, the people asked about wine and gambling, and the answer in 2:219 said that there is great sin and some benefit in them. Some drank, and then one of the emigrants led the Maghrib prayer while drunk and mixed up the recitation. The verse in 4:43 then forbade approaching prayer while drunk. Later people drank before the prayer times, and then came this verse. Abu Hurayrah and Ahmad ibn Hanbal recorded these stages. Umar bin al-Khattab asked for a clear ruling several times, and when this verse was recited to him he said, "We have abstained, we have abstained." Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi and An-Nasa'i recorded this, and At-Tirmidhi graded it sahih.

### The narrations on wine

The material gives a number of reports that were recorded by Muslim and Al-Bukhari, and by Ahmad, Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah. Umar stood on the minbar of the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah and said that the prohibition was revealed, and that wine is made from five things: grapes, dates, honey, wheat and barley. Anas reported that when the call was heard, Abu Talhah told him to spill the wine, and it flowed through the streets of Madinah. Ahmad reported the saying of the Prophet ﷺ that wine is cursed, and so are those who drink it, serve it, sell it, buy it, carry it, brew it and consume its price. Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas reported that a quarrel at a meal led to a wound on his nose.

The material also reports a saying from Abdullah bin Amr, who said that the wine prohibition was in the Tawrah. Uthman bin Affan said that wine is the mother of all sins and cannot be found together with faith, since one of them drives out the other from the heart. The report is recorded by Al-Bayhaqi.

### The inner harm of wine

The material says that wine is the root of many evils, and that it dries the spring of obedience and turns the heart away from remembrance. It says that gambling leads a man to lose everything he owns, including his family, and that it fosters malice and anger. The material says that these things are more dangerous to the soul than to the body, since the soul that is drunk with them is held back from the prayer.

### In short

- Intoxicants, gambling, the altar stones and the arrows of lots are an evil of Satan's handiwork.
- The prohibition came in stages, with the believers asking for a clear ruling until this verse came.
- The verse calls on the believers to shun these things, so that they may be successful.

91.text:
"Satan's plan is to stir up hostility and hatred between you with intoxicants and gambling and to prevent you from remembering Allah and praying. Will you not then abstain"

This verse says that Satan wants to create hostility and hatred between the believers through intoxicants and gambling, and to turn them from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. It ends by asking whether they will abstain.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Satan's plan is to stir up hostility and hatred between you with intoxicants and gambling."** The material says the harm of these things is visible in this life. Drink makes a man lose his reason, and anger and aggression follow. Gambling leaves the loser with malice towards his opponent. Qatadah is reported to have said that some Arabs would wager all they had, even their families, and then live in misery.

**"And to prevent you from remembering Allah and praying."** The material says that the spiritual harm is the greater harm, since the life of the Hereafter is the real life. A wise person takes the good and bad of that life as the true good and bad. Drinking and gambling turn the heart from remembrance and from the prayer.

**"Will you not then abstain?"** The material says that this question is a threat and a warning. It asks the believers to put an end to these things. The verse is a call to abstain, with the outcome of success.

### In short

- Satan uses wine and gambling to create hostility among the believers.
- The spiritual harm is that they turn the heart from remembrance and prayer.
- The verse ends with a question that calls for abstinence.

92.text:
"Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and beware! But if you turn away, then know that Our Messenger's duty is only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly"

This verse calls the believers to obey Allah and the Messenger, and to take care. If they turn away, the Messenger's duty is only to deliver the message clearly.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and beware!"** The material says that obedience to the Messenger is part of obedience to Allah, and that the two are tied together. The warning to beware is a call to fear the consequences of disobedience.

**"But if you turn away, then know that Our Messenger's duty is only to deliver the message clearly."** The material says that the Messenger's duty is only to convey, and that the responsibility for turning away rests with those who turn away. The material cites 5:3 for a related prohibition on the arrows, and it also says that the message is given in a clear form.

### The Messenger's duty

The material says that the verse is a comfort to the Prophet ﷺ, since his role is to deliver the message, and the response belongs to the listeners. It also says that the obedience to the Prophet ﷺ is a sign of the true faith, and that the believers should not turn away from his commands.

### In short

- Obeying Allah includes obeying the Messenger, and the believers are told to beware.
- The Messenger's duty is to deliver the message clearly.
- Turning away is the choice of the listeners, and the responsibility is theirs.

93.text:
"There is no blame on those who believe and do good for what they had consumed before ˹the prohibition˺, as long as they fear Allah, have faith, and do what is good; then they believe and act virtuously, then become fully mindful ˹of Allah˺ and do righteous deeds. For Allah loves the good-doers"

This verse says that there is no blame on those who believed and did good for what they had drunk before the prohibition, as long as they feared Allah, believed, and did good. It repeats these three stages and ends by saying that Allah loves the good-doers.

### Phrase by phrase

**"There is no blame on those who believe and do good for what they had consumed before the prohibition."** The material explains that some Companions had died while drinking wine before the prohibition, and others asked what would happen to them. The verse answers that there is no blame for what they consumed before the prohibition. The material reports the account of Anas, who said that wine was spilled in the streets of Madinah, and that the question was raised about those who had died, and the verse came. It also reports from al-Bara ibn Azib that some Companions died while drinking, and the verse answered the question about them.

**"As long as they fear Allah, have faith, and do what is good."** The material says the condition is taqwa, faith and good deeds. These are the conditions for being excused for the past.

**"Then they believe and act virtuously, then become fully mindful and do righteous deeds."** The material says that the repetition of the three stages shows that the believer must keep on with taqwa, faith and good deeds. It is a call to steadfastness.

**"For Allah loves the good-doers."** The material says that the good-doers are those who keep to taqwa and do good, and that Allah loves them.

### The lesson of the verse

The material explains that the verse removes the fear of those who had consumed wine before the prohibition, and gives them a clear path. It also makes plain that the prohibition does not depend on the past of the believer, since the past is forgiven for those who keep their faith and good deeds in the time that follows. The material cites 5:95 in the context of the hunting prohibition that follows, and it is a reminder that the legal rules of the Qur'an are set in stages.

### In short

- There is no blame for what the believers drank before the prohibition, as long as they fear Allah, believe, and do good.
- The verse answers those who asked about their companions who died before the prohibition.
- Allah loves the good-doers, and the believer must keep to taqwa and good deeds.

94.text:
"O believers! Allah will surely test you with game within the reach of your hands and spears to distinguish those who fear Him in secret. Whoever transgresses from now on will suffer a painful punishment"

This verse tells the believers that Allah will test them with game that comes within reach of their hands and their spears, so that He may know who fears Him in secret. It warns that whoever transgresses after this will suffer a painful punishment.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O believers! Allah will surely test you with game within the reach of your hands and spears."** The material explains that the test came during the pilgrimage to Hudaybiyyah, when the Muslims were in the state of ihram. Wild game and birds came close to their camp in numbers they had never seen. The material says the young and weak game could be caught with the hands, and the mature game with the spears. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid are reported to have said so.

**"To distinguish those who fear Him in secret."** The material says the purpose of the test is to see who fears Allah when He is not seen. A believer who holds back from the game when he could easily take it shows a fear of Allah that is real. The material cites 67:12, which speaks of those who fear their Lord in the unseen, for whom there is forgiveness and a great reward.

**"Whoever transgresses from now on will suffer a painful punishment."** The material says that after the prohibition has been set, whoever disobeys it will receive a painful punishment. The material reports from As-Suddi that the warning is for disobedience of the command.

### The inner test

The material explains that the test is not only in the pilgrimage. A person may have power over another, to harm his life, his wealth or his honour, and it is the one who holds back out of fear of Allah who has truly passed the test. The material says that the former will have a painful punishment, and the latter the blessings of Allah.

### In short

- The test at Hudaybiyyah was game that came close to the believers in the state of ihram.
- The purpose is to see who fears Allah when He is unseen.
- Transgression after the prohibition brings a painful punishment.

95.text:
"O believers! Do not kill game while on pilgrimage. Whoever kills game intentionally must compensate by offering its equivalence, as judged by two just men among you, to be offered at the Sacred House, or by feeding the needy, or by fasting so that they may taste the consequences of their violations. Allah has forgiven what has been done. But those who persist will be punished by Allah. And Allah is Almighty, capable of punishment"

This verse forbids the believers to kill game while they are on pilgrimage. Whoever kills game deliberately must make compensation, by an animal equal to what he killed as judged by two just men, to be offered at the Sacred House, or by feeding the needy, or by fasting. Allah forgave what was done before, but whoever persists will be punished.

### Phrase by phrase

**"O believers! Do not kill game while on pilgrimage."** The material explains that the prohibition covers the state of ihram and the sacred area around the Haram. The material says the word for killing, taqtulu, is used here and not the word for eating, so the prohibition is on killing, and eating from game killed by others is allowed for a pilgrim who did not help in the hunt. The material says the same rule is in the hadith.

**"Whoever kills game intentionally must compensate by offering its equivalence, as judged by two just men among you."** The material says that the expiation is due for a deliberate killing, and according to the majority also for a killing by mistake or by forgetting. The equivalent is set by two just Muslims. The material gives reports of the Companions: Umar told a man who had killed a deer to bring two of his brethren to judge him, and the judgement was a goat. The material says Az-Zuhri said the Qur'an mentions the expiation for deliberate killing and the sunnah extends it to the forgetful. Camels are the equivalent of ostriches, cows of wild cattle, and goats of deer. Ibn Abbas is reported to have said that where there is no equivalent, its value should be given in Makkah as charity.

**"To be offered at the Sacred House."** The material says the animal must be brought to the Ka'bah in the sacred area, slaughtered there, and its meat divided among the poor of the sacred area. The material says there is consensus on this.

**"Or by feeding the needy, or by fasting."** The material says that if the pilgrim cannot offer an equivalent, he may feed the poor. Ibn Abbas is reported to have given a scale: for an antelope, a sheep or six poor people fed, or three days of fasting; for a deer, a cow or twenty poor fed or twenty days of fasting; for an ostrich, a camel or thirty poor fed or thirty days of fasting. The material says the measure of food for each poor person is a mudd. The material says the weight of half a sa' is about 1.62 kilograms and that the expiation may be paid in grain at that rate.

**"So that they may taste the consequences of their violations."** The material says the expiation is so that the person feels the weight of his error.

**"Allah has forgiven what has been done. But those who persist will be punished by Allah."** The material explains that what was done before the prohibition, in the time of ignorance, is forgiven. Whoever repeats the offence after the prohibition is punished by Allah, and must pay the expiation again. The material reports that Ata' said there is no punishment from the authorities for it, since it is a sin between the person and Allah, and he must pay the expiation.

**"And Allah is Almighty, capable of punishment."** The material says that Allah is the one who requites the wrongdoer.

### The reading of the verse

The material says that the verse was revealed about a man from the Companions who killed game and forgot that he was in ihram. The reports say that the Companions in the time of the Prophet ﷺ took the same rule for those who forgot. The material says the expiation is due in every case, whether first, second or third, deliberate or accidental.

### In short

- The pilgrim in ihram must not kill game, and whoever kills it deliberately must make compensation.
- The compensation is an equal animal judged by two just men, brought to the Ka'bah, or the feeding of the poor, or fasting.
- Allah forgave what was done in the time of ignorance, and whoever repeats the offence will be punished.

96.text:
"It is lawful for you to hunt and eat seafood, as a provision for you and for travellers. But hunting on land is forbidden to you while on pilgrimage. Be mindful of Allah to Whom you all will be gathered"

This verse makes lawful for the believers the hunting and eating of sea game, as a provision for them and for travellers. It forbids hunting on land while they are on pilgrimage, and it ends by urging them to fear Allah, before whom they will be gathered.

### Phrase by phrase

**"It is lawful for you to hunt and eat seafood, as a provision for you and for travellers."** The material explains that sea game is lawful, and it names two kinds. The first is what is taken from the water alive, and the second is what the water throws ashore dead, and which is lawful to eat when salted. Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, Zayd ibn Thabit, Abdullah ibn Amr, Ikrimah, Mujahid, As-Suddi and Al-Hasan al-Basri are reported to have said similar things. The material cites a report from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said that an army of three hundred men under Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah ate from a huge fish that the sea had cast ashore for eighteen days, and that two of its ribs were set in the ground and a camel passed beneath them. The report is recorded in the two sahihs.

**"But hunting on land is forbidden to you while on pilgrimage."** The material says that the hunting of land game is forbidden in ihram. Whoever hunts while in ihram must pay the expiation, along with the sin if he does it deliberately, as the earlier verse 5:95 set out. The material says the meat of game killed by mistake is not lawful to eat, and that the game killed for a pilgrim is not lawful to him in particular.

**"And if you are a pilgrim, the game is lawful when another hunts it."** The material gives two reports. As-Sa'b ibn Jaththamah gave a zebra to the Prophet ﷺ, and he returned it, saying that they were in ihram. In another report, Abu Qatadah hunted a zebra while not in ihram, and the Prophet ﷺ asked whether anyone had pointed at it or helped kill it, and when they said no, he said to eat. The material says these reports are in the two sahihs.

**"Be mindful of Allah to Whom you all will be gathered."** The material says that the verse ends with the reminder of return to Allah, and that the believers must obey what He commands and avoid what He forbids.

### The water of the sea

The material says that Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib explained the first part of the verse as the fresh game taken from the sea and the second part as the salted food, and the material notes that Ibn Abbas read the water game as what is taken alive from the water. Malik ibn Anas recorded that Abu Hurayrah said a man asked the Prophet ﷺ whether a believer at sea could use the sea water for ablution, since their fresh water runs short and they grow thirsty. The Prophet ﷺ said that its water is pure and its dead are lawful. Ash-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal recorded it with the four Sunan compilers, and Al-Bukhari, At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Hibban graded it sahih. The material says that Ibn Jarir, At-Tabari, read the verse as the broad permission for the people of the sea.

### In short

- Sea game is lawful as food for the believers and for travellers.
- The hunting of land game is forbidden in the state of ihram, and the expiation is due for it.
- The believers must fear Allah, to whom they will return.

97.text:
"Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a sanctuary of well-being for all people, along with the sacred months, the sacrificial animals, and the offerings decorated with garlands. All this so you may know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and that He has perfect knowledge of everything"

This verse says that Allah made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a sanctuary of well-being for all people, along with the sacred months, the sacrificial animals and the garlanded offerings. It says that all this is so that the believers may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and on the earth, and has perfect knowledge of everything.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, a sanctuary of well-being for all people."** The material explains that the word qiyam means that on which the stability and survival of something depends. The Ka'bah is the cause of the stability and tranquility of the people. The material says that as long as people turn towards it in prayer and the hajj continues, the world will remain safe, and that if no one made the hajj or turned towards it, the world would face a great punishment. Ata' is reported to have called the Ka'bah the deep sea that holds the world. The material says that this link is known through the spirit and through the long experience of peace in Makkah, and that the cause of this is known only through the words of the Creator.

**"Along with the sacred months, the sacrificial animals, and the offerings decorated with garlands."** The material says that these four things are a sanctuary and a sign for the Arabs, who regarded them as sacred even in the time of ignorance. The Ka'bah and the sacred area were made a haram, where hunting and the cutting of trees and grass are forbidden. The sacred months are the months when fighting is forbidden. The offerings and the garlanded animals were symbols of the sanctity of the pilgrimage.

**"All this so you may know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth."** The material says this knowledge is the purpose of the sanctuary. The One who made these things for the benefit of mankind knows the good of their lives, and He will count their deeds and reward them.

**"And that He has perfect knowledge of everything."** The material says that none of the deeds or affairs of the people escape the observation of Allah, and He will repay each one for good or evil.

### The sanctuary and peace

The material says that peace in the world comes from laws and their enforcement, and that the Ka'bah is a symbol and a means of peace, since in the sacred area even the strong cannot oppress the weak. The material reflects that the rites are signs of the trial of man, not sources of holiness in themselves, and that they remind the believer that God sees all his actions.

### In short

- The Ka'bah, the sacred months, the sacrificial animals and the garlanded offerings are a sanctuary for mankind.
- The purpose is to show that Allah has perfect knowledge of the heavens and the earth.
- The sanctuary is a sign of peace, and the rites are a sign of trial, not of holiness in themselves.

98.text:
"Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that He is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful"

This verse tells the believers that Allah is severe in punishment, and that He is also All-Forgiving and Most Merciful.

### Phrase by phrase

**"Know that Allah is severe in punishment."** The material says that the laws of lawful and unlawful are based on wisdom, and that whoever obeys them receives good, while whoever opposes them receives the worst of curse and punishment. The warning in this phrase is that Allah's punishment is severe.
